13:1: Abu Ja`far said: We have already explained the interpretation of His statement: Alif, Lam, Ra, and Alif, Lam, Ra, and their counterparts from the letters of the alphabet with which the beginnings of some of the chapters of the Qur’an are opened, in what has passed, sufficient to repeat them, except that we will mention from the narration what came specifically for each chapter that began its beginning with something from it. What came in the narration about that in this surah from Ibn Abbas from the transmission of Abu al-Dhaha Muslim bin Subayh and Saeed bin Jubair from him, is the distinction between the meaning of what began with it at the beginning, with the addition of the meem in it over the rest of the surahs with alif-l-ra, and the meaning of what began with its sisters, with that being missing from it. He mentioned the narration about it: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Al-Mar, he said: I am God, I see. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: The bitter, he said: I am God, I see. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid: Al-Mar is an opening with which he begins his speech. And His saying: These are the verses of the Book, the Most High says: Those whose story I have told you are the verses of the Book that I revealed before this Book that I revealed to you, to those to whom I revealed it from among My messengers before you. It was said: He meant the Torah and the Gospel. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: These are the verses of the Book, the books that came before the Qur’an. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid: These are the verses of the Book, he said: the Torah and the Gospel. And His saying: And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, the Qur’an, so act according to what is in it and hold fast to it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid: And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, he said: the Qur’an. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, meaning: this Qur’an. In his saying: And He who revealed to you, there are two aspects of parsing: One of them: raising, as it is a new statement, so it is raised by the truth and the truth by it. And on this face is the interpretation of Mujahid and Qatada which we mentioned before from them. The other: the lowering, in conjunction with the Book, so the meaning of the speech then is: those are the verses of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an. Then he begins: the truth, meaning: that truth, so its raising is by an implied part of the speech, which is dispensed with by the apparent meaning of it. And if it is said: The meaning of that is: Those are the verses of the Book that was revealed to you from your Lord, the truth, and the waw was only inserted in and which, and it is a description of the Book, just as the poet inserted it in his saying: To the honorable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded place So, the conjunction with the letter waw, and all of that is from the description of one, was a way of interpretation. But if that is interpreted in this way, then the correct reading in truth is the accusative, as it is an attribute of the one who. And His saying: But most people do not believe, but most of the people from the polytheists of your people do not believe in the truth that was revealed to you from your Lord, and they do not acknowledge this Qur’an and the decisive verses in it.
13:2: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: God, O Muhammad, is the one who raised the seven heavens without any pillars that you can see, and made them a raised ceiling for the earth. The pillars are the plural of column, which are the masts and what the building is supported with, as Al-Nabigha said: The jinn are vile. I have given them permission to build Palmyra with stones and columns. The plural of pillar is amd, just as the plural of adeem is adam. If it is pluralized with a dammah and it is said amad, it is permissible, just as the plural of messenger is rusul, and thankfulness is thankfulness. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of His statement: He raised the heavens without pillars that you can see. Some of them said: The interpretation of that is: God is the One who raised the heavens with pillars that you do not see. Who said that? Ahmad bin Hisham told us, he said, Muadh bin Muadh told us, he said, Imran bin Hudayr told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: So-and-so says that it is on pillars, meaning the sky. He said: He said: Read it: without pillars that you see it, meaning: you do not see it. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Muadh bin Muadh told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hadir, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Hammad told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Without intention that you see it, he said: With intention that you do not see it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Without pillars that you see, he said: It is: you do not see it. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Unintentionally, he says: intentionally, you do not see it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Ishaq told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatada, regarding his statement: God is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, Qatada said: Ibn Abbas said: With pillars, but you cannot see them. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, he said: How do you know? Perhaps it is with pillars that you cannot see. Whoever interprets this in this way intends the Arabs’ approach of presenting denial from the end of a word to its beginning, like the poet’s saying: I do not see her still being unjust, causing me misfortune and resentment. He wants: I see that she is still unjust, so he presented the denial from its place from the word still, and as the other said: If you like the state of a person's life, leave him and live by his condition and the nights. They come back to what is good for them, even if it is something that people do not see as a tool. Meaning: Even if people see him as someone who does not spare any effort. Others said: Rather, it was raised unintentionally. Who said that? Muhammad bin Khalaf Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Adam told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Iyas bin Muawiyah, regarding his statement: He raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, he said: The sky is vaulted over the earth like a dome. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Without you seeing it, without intention, he said: He raised it without intention. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings about this is to say as God Almighty said: God is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, so they are raised without pillars that we can see, as our Lord, may His praise be glorified, said, and there is no report other than that, nor is there any proof that must be accepted by the saying of anyone other than Him. As for his saying: Then He rose above the Throne, it means: He rose above it. We have explained the meaning of istiwa’, the differences of those who differed about it, and the correct statement in what they said about it, with its evidence in what has passed, so that there is no need to repeat it in this place. And His saying: And He subjected the sun and the moon, meaning: He made the sun and the moon move in the sky and subjected them therein for the interests of His creation, and He made them subservient to their benefits, so that they might know by their movement therein the number of years and the reckoning, and by it they might separate between night and day. And His saying: Everything runs for a specified term, God Almighty says: All of that runs in the heavens, for a specified term, meaning: for a known time, and that is until the end of the world and the Day of Resurrection, when the sun will be rolled up, the moon will be eclipsed, and the stars will be extinguished. This was omitted from the speech, so that the listeners from the people of the language in whose language the Qur’an was revealed would understand its meaning, and that all must be added to what surrounds it. And similar to what we said about his statement: for a specified term, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term, he said: the world. And His saying: He directs the matter, the Most High says: God, who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, decrees all the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, and He directs all of that alone, without partner, supporter, or helper. Glory be to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He manages the matter, he decides it alone. He said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. And His statement: He details the verses, meaning: Your Lord details the verses of His Book for you, making them clear to you, as an argument against you, O people, that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord, meaning: that you may fulfill your meeting with God and the return to Him, so that you may believe in His promise and His threat, and refrain from worshipping gods and idols, and devote your worship to Him if you are certain of that. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Perhaps you will be certain of the meeting with your Lord, and God, Blessed and Exalted be He, only revealed His Book and sent His Messengers so that we would believe in His promise and be certain of meeting Him.
13:3: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And God is He who spread out the earth, extending it in length and breadth. And His saying: And He placed therein firm mountains, means that He, the Most High, says: And He placed firm mountains on the earth. Rawasi is the plural of rasiya, which means fixed. It is said: I anchored the peg in the ground, if I fixed it, as the poet said: By the immortals, what they throw away, and the lifeless and disheveled, the newborn has established it in the index It means: I proved it. And His saying: And rivers, means: And He made rivers of water in the earth. And his saying: And of all the fruits He has made therein two mates, so the min in his saying: And of all the fruits He has made therein two mates, is a connection to made, the second, not the first. The meaning of the words: And He made therein two mates of every fruit. By two mates, He meant two of every male, and two of every female. So that is four, two of the males, and two of the females, according to some of them. We have previously explained that the Arabs call two al-Nas 114:two spouses, and one male is a spouse for his female, and likewise one female is a spouse, and a wife for her male, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. This is further clarified by the words of God Almighty: And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, so He called the two, the male and the female, two mates. What he meant by his saying: two pairs are two types and two kinds. And his saying: The night covers the day, he says: The night covers the day and dresses it in its darkness, and the day covers the night with its light, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: The night covers the day, meaning: the night covers the day. And His saying: Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought, the Most High says: In what I have described and mentioned of the wonders of God’s creation and the great power with which He created these things, there are indications, arguments, and sermons for a people who give thought to them, so they infer and take heed from them, and they know that worship is not suitable and is not permissible except for the One Who created and managed it, without other gods and idols that are not able to harm or benefit, nor for anything other than Him, except for the One Who created that and brought it into being from nothing, Blessed and Exalted be He - and that the power with which He created that is the power with which it is not difficult for Him to revive those who perished after Him, and to restore what has perished from it, and to innovate whatever He wills to innovate - with it.
13:4: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, and on the earth there are tracts of land close together, close together, some of them close to each other by proximity, and they differ in their differentiation despite their proximity and closeness to each other. So there is a salt marsh tract that does not grow anything, next to a good tract that grows and is beneficial. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, he said: salt marshes and fresh water, salty water and fresh water. Ahmad bin Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, he said: salt marshes and barren lands. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, he said, Ishaq bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, he said: The fresh water and the salt marsh. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, meaning salty land and fresh land, they are both neighboring, with some being more nutritious than others. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said: Plots adjacent to each other, the fresh water and the salt marsh, all adjacent to each other, one grows and the other next to it does not grow. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his saying: adjacent plots, its good and fresh parts, and its bad parts are salt marshes. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, villages that are close to each other, neighboring each other. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, he said: neighboring villages. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Kufi, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: adjacent plots, he said: salty land, followed by fresh land. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, meaning salty land and fresh land, neighboring one another. Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, he said: The earth produces sweet things, and the earth produces sour things, and they are neighboring and watered with one water. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And on the earth are adjacent plots, he said: This one is sweet and this one is sour, and it is watered with one water, and they are adjacent. Abdul Jabbar bin Yahya Al-Ramli told me, he said, Damrah bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, regarding his statement: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, he said: Sweet and salty. And His statement: “And gardens of grapes and crops and palm trees, some of them in pairs and others not in pairs, watered with the same water. And We make some of them excel others in taste,” the Most High says: And on the earth, with the different meanings of saltiness and sweetness, badness and goodness, despite their proximity and closeness to one another, are gardens of grapes and crops and palm trees also, similar in creation, different in tastes and colors, while all of them come together for one drink. So some of them have a pleasant taste, a pleasant appearance and a pleasant smell, and some of them have a sour taste and no smell. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement: And gardens of grapes and crops and palm trees, in pairs and not in pairs, he said: Together and not together, watered with one water and We make some of them superior to others in taste, he said: One land contains peaches and pears and white and black grapes, and some of them bear more fruit than others, and some of them are sweet, and some of them are sour, and some of them are better than others. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: and gardens, he said: and what is with them. Al-Muntha told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid - Al-Muthanna said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. The readings differed regarding his saying: and crops and palm trees. The majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: And crops and palm trees, in the accusative case, in apposition to grapes, meaning: And on the earth are adjacent plots and gardens of grapes, crops, and palm trees. Some of the people of Basra read it as: And crops and palm trees, in the nominative case, in apposition to the gardens, meaning: And on the earth are adjacent plots, and gardens of grapes, and in it also are crops and palm trees. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings with similar meanings, and each one of them was recited by well-known people, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. This is because if the crops and palm trees are in orchards, then they are in the earth, and if they are in the earth, then the earth in which they are is a paradise, so it is the same whether they are described as being in an orchard or in the earth. As for his saying: And palm trees of different types and different types. The word sanwan is the plural of sanw, which means palm trees that share one root. There is no difference between the plural and the dual except in the case of the letter nun, which is that the letter nun in the dual is always broken, and in the plural it is continuous in all the cases of inflection. Its counterpart is qanawan, the singular of which is qanaw. And similar to what we said about the meaning of sinwan, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’: Two in pairs, he said: the one gathered, not two in pairs, the one separated. Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: Sanawan is the palm tree that has palm trees next to it at its base, and other than Sanawan is the palm tree alone. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib: Two and not two, he said: Two are the two palm trees with one root, and not two, is the palm tree and the two separate palm trees. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: I heard al-Bara’ say about this verse, he said: The palm tree has palm trees, and not in pairs, the scattered palm trees. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Amr bin Al-Haitham Abu Qatan, Yahya bin Abbad, and Affan told us - and the wording is Abu Qatan’s wording - he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, regarding his statement: In pairs and not in pairs, he said: The pair is the palm tree next to the palm trees, and not in pairs means the scattered ones. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, regarding his statement: Two in pairs and not in pairs, he said: The two in pairs are the three, four, and two palm trees whose root is one, and not in pairs means the scattered ones. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan and Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, regarding his statement: Two in pairs and not in pairs, he said: The two palm trees have one root, and not in pairs, means the separated. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: two pairs, meaning: together. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And palm trees of two types and those without two types, he means by two types: the palm tree from whose root other palm trees emerge, some of which bear fruit and some of which do not, so its root is one but its tops are scattered. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: in pairs and not in pairs, the palm trees are from one root, and not in pairs, the scattered palm trees. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And palm trees in pairs and not in pairs, he said: Together and not together. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Nafili told us, he said, Zuhair told us, he said, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Baraa, he said: The Sunwan is that which has one origin and is scattered, other than the Sunwan, which grows alone. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his saying: two in pairs, two palm trees or more from one root, and not two in pairs, is alone. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: two in pairs, two palm trees or more from one root, and not two in pairs, one. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki` told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Two and not two, he said: Two is the one, its origin is one, and not two is the one whose origin is dispersed. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: two in kind and not two in kind, he said: two in kind is the one that is united and whose origin is one, and not two in kind is the dispersed. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And palm trees in pairs and not in pairs. As for in pairs, it means two or three palm trees whose roots are one and their branches are different. And not in pairs means a single palm tree. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Two and not two. He said: Two is the palm tree that has two or three palm trees at its base, their base being one. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And palm trees in pairs and not in pairs, he said: The two in pairs are the two or three palm trees that are on one root, so people consider them to be in pairs. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, a man told me: “There was a discussion between Umar ibn al-Khattab and al-Abbas, so al-Abbas hurried to him. Umar came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, did you not see what al-Abbas did to me and what he did? I wanted to respond to him, but I remembered his position with you, so I held back. He said: May God have mercy on you, a man’s paternal uncle is like his father.” Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Two palm trees means a palm tree that has two or three palm trees at its base, the base of which is one. He said: “There was a discussion between Umar bin Al-Khattab and Al-Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, so Al-Abbas hurried to him, so Umar came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, did you not see what Al-Abbas did to me and what he did? I wanted to respond to him, but I remembered his position with you, so I held back at that. He said: May God have mercy on you, a man’s paternal uncle is like his father.” He said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Shabur, on the authority of Mujahid: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are hurting me regarding al-Abbas, for he is the remnant of my fathers, and a man’s paternal uncle is like his father.” Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’ and Ibn Abi Malekah: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar: O Umar, do you not know that a man’s paternal uncle is like his father?” Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza told me, on the authority of Mujahid: Two of two, he said: On one root are three palm trees, like three sons of a mother and a father who differ in their deeds just as the fruit of these three palm trees on one root differs. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: Like the example of the righteous and wicked sons of Adam, their father is one. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr bin Abdullah told me, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told me, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: This is a parable that God has given for the hearts of the children of Adam. The earth was in the hand of the Most Gracious as a single clay, then He spread it out and leveled it, so the earth became adjacent pieces. Then water descends upon it from the sky, and this one produces its flowers, fruits, and trees, and its plants and revives its dead parts, and this one produces its saltwater, salt and filth, and both are watered by one water. If the water were salty, it would be said: This one became salty because of the water! Thus people were created from Adam, so a reminder descends upon them from the sky, so their hearts are softened and become humble and submissive, and their hearts become hardened and become distracted and forgetful and become harsh. Al-Hasan said: By God, no one sits with the Qur’an except that he rises from it with an addition or a subtraction. God says: And We send down of the Qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy to the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss. And his saying: It is watered with one water. The readings differed regarding his saying: It is watered. The majority of the people of Medina and Iraq, including the people of Kufa and Basra, read it as: tasqa with a ta meaning: the gardens, crops, and palm trees are watered. Some of them used to say: tasqa was said with a ta because grapes are feminine. Some of the Meccans and Kufians read it as yasqa with a ya. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for its being masculine if it is read in this way. Rather, it is a report about the gardens, grapes, palm trees, and crops, that they are watered with one water. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: If it is read with a taa, then it refers to grapes, as cattle were mentioned in His statement: from what is in their bellies, and then feminized, saying: and upon it and upon the ships you are carried. So whoever says: is watered with a yaa, then he made grapes one of those that are masculine and feminine like cattle. Some grammarians of Kufa said: Whoever says: is watered means that the crops, gardens, and palm trees are feminine, and whoever says: is watered means that all of that is watered with one water, and its food is different, sour and sweet, so in this there is a sign. Abu Ja`far said: The reading that I like the most is the reading of the one who reads it with the letter ta`: tasqa bi-ma` wahid, meaning: the gardens, palm trees and crops are watered with one water, because tasqa came after what was mentioned, and it is a group of people other than the children of Adam. The other interpretation is not impossible, meaning: yasqa bi-ma` wahid, meaning: all of that is watered with one fresh water, not salty. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: They are watered with one water, the water of the sky, is like the example of the righteous and wicked children of Adam, their father is one. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: It is watered with one water, he said: Rainwater. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Kufi, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, it is watered with one water, he said: rain water. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Ibn Jurayj read it, on the authority of Mujahid: It is watered with one water, he said: the water of the sky, like the example of the righteous and wicked children of Adam, their father is one. He said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Abdul Jabbar bin Yahya Al-Ramli told us, he said, Damrah bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab: It is watered with one water, he said: with rain water. And his saying: And We give some of them preference over others in eating, the reading of that differed. The majority of the Meccans, Medinans, Basrans, and some Kufians read it as and we prefer, with a nun, meaning: and we prefer some of them over others in eating. The general reading of the Kufians is: And it is preferred, with the letter ya, in response to his saying: The night covers the day, and some of them are preferred over others. Abu Ja`far said: They are two widely-used readings with one meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. However, I like the ya’ more in the reading because it is in the context of a statement that begins with: God is He who raised the heavens, so reading it with ya’, since that is the case, is more appropriate. The meaning of the words: The gardens of grapes, crops, and palm trees, both in pairs and not in pairs, are watered with one fresh water, not salt. God varies the tastes of these, making some of them superior to others in taste, so this one is sweet and this one is sour. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We prefer some of them over others in taste, he said: Persian and date palms, sweet and sour. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr: And We prefer some of them over others in eating. He said: The same land contains peaches, pears, white and black grapes, and some of them bear more fruit than others, and some of them are sweet and some of them are sour, and some of them are better than others. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amer Abu Al-Nu’man told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And We prefer some of them over others in eating, he said: Barni and so-and-so, and some of this is better than some. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And We prefer some of them over others in taste, he said: This is sour, this is sweet, and this is bitter. Mahmoud bin Khidash told me, he said, Saif bin Muhammad, the nephew of Sufyan al-Thawri, told us, he said, al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding his statement: And We prefer some of them over others in taste, he said: Dates and Persian dates, sweet and sour. Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Tirmidhi told us, he said, Sulayman bin Ubayd God Al-Raqi told us, he said, Ubayd God bin Amr Al-Raqi told us, on the authority of Zayd bin Abi Anisa, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And We prefer some of them over others in taste, he said: Dates and Persian dates, sweet and sour. And His saying: Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason, the Most High says: In the contradiction of God Almighty between these adjacent pieces of land and the fruits of their gardens and their crops in what we have described and explained, there is clear evidence and a lesson for a people who reason about the difference of that, that the one who contradicted between them in this manner in which he contradicted between them is the one who contradicted between His creation in what He has apportioned to them of guidance and misguidance, success and failure. So He guided this one and failed that one, and guided this one and established that one. And if He had willed, He would have made all of them equal, just as if He had willed to make equal all the eaters of the fruits of Paradise who drink the same drink and are watered the same watering, and they are different in eating.
13:5: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And if you wonder, O Muhammad, at these polytheists who have taken as gods that neither harm nor benefit them to worship besides Me, “then wonder at their saying: ‘When we are dust,’ and have decayed and become nothing, ‘shall we then be in a new creation?’ We will indeed be recreated and recreated anew as we were before our death, as a denial of God’s power and a denial of reward, punishment, and resurrection after death, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “And if you are amazed, then be amazed.” If you are amazed, O Muhammad, then be amazed at their saying, ‘When we are dust, will we then be in a new creation?’ The Most Merciful, Blessed and Exalted, was amazed at their denial of resurrection after death. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And if you are amazed, then be amazed at their statement, he said: If you are amazed at their denial, and they have seen of God’s power and command and what He has set forth for them of examples, then He showed them of the life of the dead in the dead land, if you are amazed at this then be amazed at their statement, When we are dust, will we then be in a new creation? Do they not see that We created them from a sperm-drop? So creation from a sperm-drop is more difficult, or creation from dust and bones? The scholars of Arabic differed regarding the reason for repeating the question in his statement: Are we indeed in a new creation? after the first question in his statement: Should we be dust? Some of the Basran scholars said: The first is a circumstance, and the second is what the interrogative falls on, as you say: Is Zaid leaving on Friday? He said: And whoever places another interrogative on his saying: If we are dust, made it a circumstance for something mentioned before it, as if it was said to them: Will you be resurrected? So they said: If we are dust? Then he made this another interrogative. He said: This is far-fetched. He said: If you wish, you may not make your saying: If an interrogative, and make the interrogative in the wording on we, as if you said: Is Abdullah leaving on Friday? And you implied its negation. This is a place where you did not begin with If, and it is not common in speech. If he said: Today Abdullah is leaving, it would not be good, but it is permissible. The Arabs have said: I did not know that he is righteous, meaning: He is righteous as I know. Another said: If is a condition, and not a time, and what comes after it is an answer to it, if there is no question in the second, the meaning is for it, because it is what is required. He said: Don’t you see that you say: If you stand, Zaid will stand, and he will stand? Whoever puts it in the subjunctive mood, it is because it is the answer to the condition, and whoever puts it in the nominative case, it is because the question is for him, and he cited as evidence the saying of the poet: I swore to him that if night falls, one of my houses will still be in front of you. So the answer to the oath was made jussive because it was the answer to the conditional clause, and the correct way is to raise it. He said: This is how this verse is. He said: And whoever inserted the question a second time, it was because it is the one that is relied upon, and he left out the first conditional clause. And His statement: Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, the Most High says: These are the ones who denied the resurrection and rejected the reward and punishment, and said: When we are dust, shall we then be in a new creation? They are the ones who denied the power of their Lord and denied His Messenger, and they are the ones who will have shackles around their necks on the Day of Resurrection in the fire of Hell. So those are the companions of the Fire, meaning: they are the inhabitants of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. They will abide therein, meaning: they will remain therein forever, they will not die in it nor will they emerge from it.
13:6: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And they hasten you, O Muhammad, the polytheists of your people, with affliction and punishment before prosperity and well-being, so they say: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment, and they know what happened to the nations before them who disobeyed their Lord and denied His messengers of God's punishments and great affliction, so among them was a nation transformed into apes and another into pigs, and among them was a nation destroyed by earthquake and another by sinking. And that is the examples, about which God Almighty said: And there have already been examples before them. And Al-Mithlaat are the severe punishments, and the singular of them is Mithla, with the first letter open and the second letter closed, then the plural is Mithlaat, just as the singular of charity is Sadaqah, then the plural is Sadaqat. It was mentioned that Tamim among the Arabs add the second letter and the third together from Mithlaat, so the singular of them in their language is Mithla, then the plural is Mithlaat, like Ghurfa and Ghurafaat. The verb from it is: I compared it to Amthal Mithlaan, with the first letter open and the third letter closed. So if you mean that you cut it off from someone else, you say: I compared it to his companion Amthalhu Imthalan, and that is if you cut it off from him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And there have already been examples before them, the incidents of God among the nations before you. And his statement: And they hasten you to do evil before good, and they are the polytheists of the Arabs, they hastened evil before good, and they said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And they urge you to hasten the evil before the good, he said: the punishment before the well-being, and before them there have been examples, he said: the punishments. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: The examples, he said: The examples. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And there have already been examples before them, he said: The examples are what God has given the nations as examples of the punishment with which He has inflicted them. The examples of the punishment have passed away before them, and they have known that, and what God has given them as examples when they disobeyed Him and disobeyed His messengers has come to pass. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Salim told us, he said, I heard Al-Sha’bi say regarding His statement: And before them there have been examples, he said: The monkeys and pigs are the examples. And His statement: And indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, the Most High says: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is the Possessor of concealment of the sins of those among the people who repent from their sins, so He will leave them exposed for them on the Day of Resurrection, and He will pardon them for their punishment for it sooner or later, for their wrongdoing, meaning: for their doing what they did without My permission for them to do it, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty, for whoever perishes while persisting in his sins on the Day of Resurrection, if He does not hasten that for him in this world, or gather them for him in this world and the Hereafter. Abu Ja`far said: Although this statement appears to be a report, it is a threat from God and a warning to the polytheists among the people of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, if they do not repent and turn from their disbelief before God’s vengeance befalls them. Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people, he says: But your Lord.
13:7: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve say, O Muhammad, from your people, Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord? Why has a sign not been sent down to Muhammad from his Lord? They mean a sign and proof for his prophethood, and that is their saying: Why has a treasure not been sent down to him or an angel not come with him?. God says: O Muhammad, You are only a warner, to them, warning them of God's punishment that will befall them because of their polytheism, And for every people is a guide, meaning: And for every people there is an imam whom they follow, and a guide who precedes them and guides them either to good or to evil. Its origin is from: Hadi Al-Faras, which is its neck that guides the rest of its body. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, with their differences regarding the meaning of the guide in this place. Some of them said: He is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And those who disbelieve say, ‘Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?’ This is what the polytheists of the Arabs said. God said: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide. Every people has a caller who calls them to God. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Mansur, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide. They said: Muhammad is the warner, and he is the guide. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. Others said: What is meant by the guide in this place is: God. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide. He said: Muhammad is the warner, and God is the guide. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, he said: Muhammad is the warner, and God is the guide. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubair: You are only a warner, he said: You, O Muhammad, are a warner, and God is the guide. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, he said: The warner is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. For every people there is a guide, he said: God is the guide of every people. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, meaning: You, O Muhammad, are a warner, and I am the guide of every people. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide. The warner is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the guide is God Almighty. Others said that Al-Hadi, in the same place, means: Prophet. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Mundhir said, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, And for every people there is a guide, he said: A prophet. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, he said: A prophet. He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, he said: For every people there is a prophet, and the warner is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said, Muhammad bin Al-A’la told us, he said, Abdul Malik told me, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And for every people there is a guide, he said: A prophet. He said, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And for every people there is a guide, meaning: for every people there is a prophet. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And for every people there is a guide, he said: A prophet. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And for every people there is a guide, he said: A prophet who calls them to God. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And for every people is a guide, he said: For every people is a prophet. The guide is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the warner is also the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he recited: And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them, and he said: A warner from the first warners, he said: A prophet from the prophets. Others said: Rather, he meant by it: Every people has a leader. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide. He said: You, O Muhammad, are only a warner, and for every people there are leaders. He said, Al-Ashja’i told us, he said, Ismail told me - and: Sufyan: on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih: And for every people there is a guide, he said: Every people have leaders. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide. He said: The guide is the leader, and the leader is the imam, and the imam is the action. Al-Hasan told me, he said, Muhammad told us - and he is Ibn Yazid - on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Rafi’ regarding his statement: You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, he said: A leader. Others said: He is Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Who said that? Ahmad bin Yahya al-Sufi told us, al-Hasan bin al-Husayn al-Ansari told us, Muadh bin Muslim Bayaa al-Harawi told us, on the authority of Ata bin al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse, You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed his hand on his chest and said: I am the warner, and for every people there is a guide, and he pointed with his hand to Ali’s shoulder and said: You are the guide, O Ali, through you the guided ones after me will be guided. Others said: It means: Every people has a caller. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And for every people there is a guide, he said: a caller. I have explained the meaning of guidance, and that it is the followed Imam who leads the people. If that is the case, then it is possible that it is God who guides His creation, and His creation follows His guidance, and they follow His commands and prohibitions. It is possible that he is the Prophet of God who is followed by his nation. It is permissible for him to be an imam who is followed and whose method and approach are followed by his companions. It is possible that he is a preacher of good or evil. Since this is the case, there is no more correct statement about this than to say as God Almighty said: Muhammad is the warner to whom he was sent with the warning, and every people has a guide who guides them, so they follow him and imitate him.
13:8: Abu Ja`far said: The Almighty says: "And if you are amazed, then amazed is their saying: 'When we are dust, shall we then be in a new creation?'" They deny the ability of God to bring them back as a new creation after their annihilation and affliction, but they do not deny His ability to originate them and form them in the wombs, and to manage them and direct them in them from one state to another. So He began the report about that from the beginning, and the meaning is what I described, so He, the Most High, said: God knows what every female carries and what the wombs absorb and what they increase. He says: And what the wombs absorb from their pregnancy in the nine months to complete their sending of menstrual blood, and what they increase, in their pregnancy over the nine months to complete what was reduced from the pregnancy in the nine months by sending menstrual blood, and everything with Him is by measure. Nothing of His measure exceeds His measure, and nothing that He wills and manages falls short of His management, just as a female's pregnancy does not increase beyond what He has determined for it of pregnancy, nor does it fall short of what He has determined for it of measure. And the amount, is a verbal noun from the word qadar. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub bin Mahan told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Malik told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He knows what every female carries and what the wombs absorb, he said: If a woman sees blood for a day after her pregnancy, the pregnancy increases by a day. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: God knows what every female carries and what the wombs absorb and what they add, meaning the miscarriage, and what they gain, meaning what the womb gains in pregnancy beyond what it absorbs until it gives birth to it completely. That is because some women carry their pregnancy for ten months, and some for nine months, and some for more, and some for less. That is the decrease and increase that God mentioned, and all of that is by His knowledge. Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, he said, Abdul Salam told us, he said, Khasif told us, on the authority of Mujahid, or Saeed bin Jubair, regarding the statement of God: And what the wombs decrease, he said: Its decrease is less than nine, and the increase is more than nine. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: Al-Ghaydh is what the pregnant woman sees of blood during her pregnancy, so it is a deficiency in the child, and the increase is what is more than nine months, so it is the completion of the deficiency, and it is an increase. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Samad told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And the wombs do not decrease or increase, he said: What you see of blood, and what increases beyond nine months. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: He knows what the wombs decrease and what they increase. He said: What exceeds nine months. And what the wombs decrease, he said: The blood that a woman sees during her pregnancy. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn and Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, they said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And the wombs do not decrease nor increase, he said: Al-Ghayd is when a pregnant woman sees blood during her pregnancy, so it is al-Ghayd, and it is a decrease in the child. And whatever exceeds nine months is the completion of that decrease, which is the increase. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Abd al-Salam told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: And the wombs do not decrease nor increase, he said: If she sees less than nine, then it increases over nine like the days of menstruation. Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the wombs do not decrease, he said: the exit of blood, and they do not increase, he said: the withholding of blood. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the wombs do not decrease means the woman’s ejaculation until the child is lost, nor does it increase he said: If the woman does not ejaculate, the child will be complete and great. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And the wombs do not decrease nor increase, he said: The woman sees blood and carries for more than nine months. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And what the wombs decrease, he said: It is the woman who sees blood during her pregnancy. He said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his saying: And the wombs do not decrease nor increase, the shedding of blood until the child is lost, and increases, if the woman does not shed blood, the child will be complete and great. He said, Al-Hakam bin Musa told us, he said, Haql told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, he said: I said to Mujahid: My wife saw blood, and I hope that she is pregnant. Abu Ja`far said: This is how it is in the Book. Mujahid said: That is the decrease in the wombs: He knows what the wombs decrease and what they increase, and everything with Him is by measure. The child continues to decrease as long as she sees blood, and when the blood stops, it increases, and it continues until it is complete. That is what He said: And the wombs decrease and what they increase, and everything with Him is by measure. He said, Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, He said, Hisham told us, He said, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And the wombs do not decrease nor increase, he said: The decrease is the pregnant woman who sees blood in her pregnancy, and it is the decrease, and it is a decrease in the child. So what exceeds nine months is the increase, and they are the completion of the birth. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding this verse: God knows what every female carries and what the wombs absorb, he said: Whenever the womb absorbs blood, that increases the pregnancy. He said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, something similar. Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibad ibn al-Awam told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ikrimah: And what the wombs decrease, he said: The decrease of the womb is the blood on the pregnancy. Whenever the womb decreases from the blood for a day, the pregnancy increases by a day, until it is completed and she is pure. He said, Abbad told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ya’la bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Al-Walid bin Saleh told us, he said, Abu Yazid told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding this verse: And what the wombs absorb, he said: It is the menstruation of the pregnancy, and what they increase, he said: So for every day she menstruates in her pregnancy, she has a day to increase in her purity, until she completes nine months pure. He said, Yazid bin Harun told us, Imran bin Hadhir told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And the wombs do not decrease or increase, he said: What she saw of blood in her pregnancy increased in her pregnancy. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And the wombs do not decrease nor increase, “do not decrease,” is less than nine, and do not increase, is more than nine. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Yahya, who said, I heard al-Dahhak say: A child may be born at two years. Al-Dahhak was born at two years. Al-Ghaydh is less than nine, and and what increases is more than nine months. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And the wombs do not decrease nor increase, he said: less than nine, and they do not increase, he said: more than nine. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: I was born at the age of two. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Yahya, he said, Ad-Dahhak told us: His mother carried him for two years. He said: And what the wombs decrease, he said: what decreases from nine, and what increases, he said: what exceeds nine. He said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: God knows what every female carries and what the wombs absorb, he said: Every female is from God’s creation. He said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak and Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hasan, they said: Ghaydh is less than nine months. He said, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Jamila bint Saad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: Pregnancy does not last more than two years, the amount of time it takes for the shadow of a spindle to turn. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi: And what the wombs absorb, he said: It is pregnancy for nine months, and less than nine, and what they increase, he said: Over nine. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Amr bin Thabit told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And what the wombs decrease, he said: The menstruation of a woman for her child. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the wombs do not decrease nor increase, he said: The decrease is the miscarriage, and do not increase, is beyond nine months. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: If a woman sees blood on her pregnancy, it is a sign of a decrease in the child’s nutrition, and it is an increase in the pregnancy. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: God knows what every female carries and what the wombs absorb and what they increase, he said: Al-Hasan used to say: Ghaydhudhu is when a woman gives birth after six months or seven months, or less than the limit. Qatada said: As for the excess, it is what exceeds nine months. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: The decrease in the womb is when she sees blood during her pregnancy. So everything in which she sees blood during her pregnancy, she increases her pregnancy like that. He said, Abdul Aziz told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: If a pregnant woman sees blood, it is more likely for the child. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the wombs do not decrease nor increase, “Downsizing” is the decrease in the term, and increase is what exceeds the term. This is because women do not give birth within one waiting period. A child is born after six months and lives, or after two years and lives, and in between. He said: And I heard Ad-Dahhak say: I gave birth after two years, and my front teeth had already grown. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And what the wombs decrease, he said: The decrease of the wombs is the shedding that women experience while pregnant. When that shedding comes, it is not counted as part of the pregnancy, and that decreases her pregnancy until that is lifted. And when that is lifted, she begins a future waiting period of nine months. As for as long as she sees blood, the wombs decrease and decrease, and the child becomes thin. So when that blood is lifted, the child grows, and her waiting period when that blood is lifted is nine months. And whatever comes before that, she does not count it, it is shedding, and that nullifies all of that. And his saying: And everything with Him has a measure. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: And everything with Him is by measure, yes, by God, He has preserved their sustenance and their life spans, and has given them a known term.
13:9: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: God knows what is hidden from you and from your sight, so you have not seen it, and what you have witnessed and witnessed with your sight. Nothing is hidden from Him, because they are His creation and His management: the Great, to whom everything is inferior, the Exalted, the One who is supreme over everything by His power. It is the interactive particle from the high, such as the close, from the near, and the close, from the near.
13:10: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: “A moderate person among you, O people, is he who keeps his speech secret, and he who speaks it openly, and he who conceals his disobedience to God in the darkness of the night, and he who is a pervert during the day,” meaning: and he who is apparent during the day in its light, nothing of that is hidden from Him. The secret of His creation and their public are the same to Him, because nothing is hidden from Him or concealed. It is said: Sarrab yasrab sarwan if it appears, as Qais bin Al-Khatim said: Wherever I go, I am not a thief, and dreams are not close He says: How did you walk at night along this long road, and you were not visible or standing out? Some of them used to say: He is the one who follows his path, meaning: in his school of thought and place. Scholars of Arabic speech differed about the term sarab. Some of them said: He is safe in his flock, with the letter seen open. Some of them said: He is safe in his flock, with a kasra on the letter seen. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: It is the same among you whether you conceal your speech or declare it, and whether you hide by night and go forth by day, meaning: He is a suspicious person who hides by night. But if he goes out during the day, people will see that he is innocent of sin. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said: And he travels during the day, is clear. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Abu Raja’, regarding his statement: It is the same among you whether he conceals his speech or declares it aloud, whether he hides it by night or goes forth by day, he said: God knows them best, whether he conceals his speech or declares it aloud, whether he hides it by night or goes forth by day. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Abu Raja: It is the same among you whether you conceal your speech or whether you declare it aloud, whether you hide your speech at night or go about your business during the day, he said: whoever hides it in his house, and goes about your business during the day, going about his business. His knowledge is one among them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: It is the same among you whether he conceals his speech or he who declares it aloud, he said: The secret and the public are the same to Him, and he who hides by night and goes forth by day, as for the one who hides, he is in his house, and as for the one who goes forth by day, he is wherever he is. The one who hides is the one in which he disappears and the one who goes forth, are the same to Him. He said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, regarding his statement: He who conceals himself at night, he said: He who is stubborn in sins, and he who is ignorant during the day, he said: He who is ignorant during the day. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Whether you conceal your speech or declare it aloud, all of that is the same to Him, the Blessed and Exalted. The secret is public to Him. His statement: And whoever hides by night and goes forth by day, meaning: in the darkness of the night, and going forth means: apparent during the day. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah: And he who travels during the day, he said: He who travels during the day. And in his saying: Whoever conceals speech, whoever declares it aloud, and whoever hides it at night, he raised the first of them by saying: the same, and the second is conjoined with the first, and the third with the second.
13:11: Abu Jaafar said: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: To God Almighty there are successive things mentioned. They said: The ha’ in His saying: To Him is from the mention of the name of God. And the angels who follow one another in succession. That is because when the angels of the night ascend during the day, the angels of the day follow them. Then when the day ends, the angels of the day ascend, then the angels of the night follow them. And they said: It was said: Mu’aqabat, and the angels, the plural of angel, masculine, not feminine, and the singular of angels is Mu’aqab, and its plural is Mu’aqaba, then its plural was made plural - I mean the plural of Mu’aqab, after it was made plural of Mu’aqaba - and it was said Mu’aqabat, just as it was said: the leaders of Sa’d, and the men of Banu so-and-so, the plural of men. His saying: From before him and from behind him, means by his saying: From before him, from in front of this one who hides at night and travels during the day, And from behind him, from behind his back. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur - meaning Ibn Zadhan - on the authority of al-Hasan regarding this verse: He has angels before him and behind him, he said: the angels. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Abdul Salam bin Saleh Al-Qushayri told us, he said, Ali bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar, on the authority of Kinanah Al-Adawi, he said: “Uthman bin Affan entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, tell me about the servant, how many angels are with him? He said: An angel on your right is responsible for your good deeds, and he is a trustee over the one on the left. So if you do a good deed, ten are recorded. And if you do a bad deed, the one on the left says to the one on the right: Write. He says: No, perhaps he will seek forgiveness from God and repent. So if he says it three times, he says: Yes, write. May God relieve us of him. What a bad companion! How little he watches God and how little he is ashamed of us. God says: Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher by him ready [to record] (10:10), and two angels before you and behind you. God says: He has guardians before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God (10:10), and an angel holding your forelock. So if you humble yourself before God, He will raise you up, and if you are arrogant, May God break your heart. And two angels are on your lips, and they do not protect you except by sending blessings upon Muhammad. And an angel is standing over your mouth, not allowing the snake to enter your mouth, and two angels are over your eyes. So these are ten angels over every human being. They descend as angels of the night upon the angels of the day, because the angels of the night are different from the angels of the day. So these are twenty angels over every human being, and Satan is during the day and his son is during the night.” Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: He has guardian angels before him and behind him, the angels, who protect him by the command of God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: He has guardians before him and behind him who guard him, he said: With every person are guardians who guard him by the command of God. He said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He has guardian angels before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God, so the guardian angels are by the command of God, and they are the angels. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They guard him by the command of God, he said: Angels guard him from before him and from behind him, and when his fate comes, they leave him.
