Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He has guardian angels before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God, so when the decree comes, they leave him alone. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding this verse, he said: The guardians. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: He has guardian angels before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God. He said: Angels. Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Ya’la told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement: He has angels who follow him, he said: The angels of the night follow the angels of the day. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: He has angels who follow him before him and behind him, these are the angels of the night who take turns among you by night and by day. And he told us that they gather at the time of the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer. And in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b: He has angels who follow him before him and a watchman behind him who guard him by the command of God. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: He has angels who follow him in succession, he said: Angels who follow him in succession. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: He has angels who follow him, before him and behind him. He said: The angels. Ibn Jurayj said: He follows him. He said: The angels follow him, night and day. It has reached us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They gather among you at the time of the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer. And his statement: They guard him from before him and from behind him, Ibn Jurayj said: It is like his statement: On the right and on the left, seated. He said: The good deeds are before him, and the bad deeds are behind him. The one on his right writes down the good deeds, and the one on his left writes down the bad deeds. Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman told us, I heard Layth narrating, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: There is no servant but that he has an angel assigned to him who protects him in his sleep and wakefulness from the jinn, humans, and vermin. Nothing of them comes to him wanting him but he says: Behind you, except something that God permits and it befalls him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He has angels before him and behind him, he said: He means the angels. Others said: Rather, what is meant by the successors in this place is the guards who take turns following the prince. Who said that? Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He has guardians before him and behind him, he said: That is a king from the kings of the world, he has guards behind him, guards behind him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: He has guardians before him and behind him, meaning the guardian of Satan, who will be his guard. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Sharqi: that he heard `Ikrimah say about this verse: He has guardian angels before him and behind him, he said: These are the princes. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Omar bin Nafi’ told us, he said: I heard Ikrimah say: He has followers before him and behind him, he said: The followers are before him and behind him. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: He has guardian angels before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God, he said: He is the ruler who is cautious of God, and they are the people of polytheism. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of this is the statement of the one who said: The ha’ in His statement: He has guardian angels, is from the one who mentioned the one in His statement: And he who is hidden by night, and that the guardian angels before him and behind him are his guards and his henchmen, as was said by the one whose statement we mentioned. We said: This is the more correct of the two interpretations, because His statement: He has successors, is closer to His statement: And he who is belittled by night, than to the Knower of the unseen, so because of its proximity to Him it is more likely to be from His mention, and that the meaning of that is this, with the indication of God’s statement: And when God intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it, that they are the ones meant by that. This is because He, the Most High, mentioned a people who disobey Him and are suspicious, who hide at night and appear during the day, and who protect themselves with guards who guard them and protection that prevents the people of His obedience from standing between them and what they do of disobeying God. Then He informed that if God, the Most High, intends evil for them, their guards will not benefit them, nor will their protection protect them. And his saying: They protect it from the command of God, the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of this letter in the same way that they differed in the interpretation of his saying: It has guardian angels. Whoever says: The angels are the guardian angels, says: Those who guard him from God’s command are also the angels. And whoever said: The guardians and executioners of the children of Adam, said: Those who protect him from the command of God, they are those guardians. They also differed on the meaning of his saying: From the command of God. Some of them said: He protected them from his command. Some of them said: They protect it from God’s command: by God’s command. It was mentioned that he said: Those who protect him are the angels, and the reason for his saying: By the command of God is to mean that their protection of him is by the command of God: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: They protect it by the command of God, meaning: by the permission of God. So the angels are by the command of God, and they are the angels. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: They protect him from the command of God, he said: The guardian angels, and their protection of him from the command of God. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, he said, Abdul Malik told me, on the authority of Ibn Ubaid God, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: He has guardians before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God, he said: The guardians are by the command of God. He said, Ali told us - meaning Ibn Abdullah Ibn Ja`far - he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He has guardians before him, guardians, and behind him, by the command of God, who protect him. He said, Abd al-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Sa`id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Jarud, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He has guardian angels before him “and behind him.” Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: He has angels before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God, he said: The angels by the command of God. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said: They protect it from the command of God, he said: The angels from the command of God. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: He has guardians before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God. He said: The guardians. He mentioned that who said that about me: They protect it by the command of God. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They protect it from the command of God, meaning: by the command of God. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They protect it from the command of God, and in some readings: by the command of God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: He has guardian angels before him and behind him, he said: With every person are guardians who protect him from the command of God. It was mentioned that he said: The guards of the sons of Adam protect him from the command of God. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They protect him from the command of God, meaning the guardian of Satan, who will have guards over him, protecting him from before him and from behind him. God the Almighty says: They protect him from My command, for if I intend evil for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector besides Him. Abu Hurairah Al-Dab’i told me, he said, or Qutaybah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sharqi, on the authority of Ikrimah: They protect him from the command of God, he said: the executioners. Others said: The meaning of this is: They protect him from the command of God, and the command of God is the jinn and whoever seeks to harm him and cause him harm before the coming of God’s judgment. So when His judgment comes, they leave him alone with it. Who said that? Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Al-Mu'tamir told us, I heard Laith narrating, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: There is no servant but that he has an angel assigned to him who protects him in his sleep and wakefulness from the jinn, humans, and vermin. Nothing of them comes to him wanting him but he says: Behind you, except something that God permits and it befalls him. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, he said, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Alahani, on the authority of Yazid bin Shuraih, on the authority of Kaab Al-Ahbar, who said: If every easy and difficult situation were revealed to the son of Adam, he would see devils on every thing of that. Had it not been that God has assigned angels to you to defend you in your food, drink, and private parts, then you would have been snatched away. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Amara bin Abi Hafsa told us, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, he said: A man from Murad came to Ali, may God be pleased with him, while he was praying, and he said: Beware, for some people from Murad want to kill you. He said: With every man are two angels who protect him as long as he is not destined, and when the destiny comes, they leave him alone with it, and the appointed time is a fortified paradise. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Dhakwan, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: There is no human being but that there is an angel assigned to him who defends him until he hands him over to the one who has been destined for him. Others said: The meaning of this is: They protect it from God. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: They protect it from the command of God, he said: They protect it from God. Abu Ja`far said: Ibn Jurayj means by his saying: They preserve it for him, the angels assigned to the son of Adam, to preserve his good and bad deeds. They are the angels who, according to us, preserve the good and bad deeds of the son of Adam by the command of God. Abu Ja`far said: According to this statement, the meaning of his saying, From the command of God, must be that the guardians are from the command of God, or are protected by the command of God. And the ha in his saying, They protect it, must be singular and mentioned, and what is meant by it are good and bad deeds, because it is a metaphor for mentioning the one who hides at night and travels during the day, and that the one who hides at night, his mention is established in place of the report about his bad and good deeds, as it was said: And ask the town in which we were and the caravan in which we came. And Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid used to say something contrary to these sayings. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And whoever hides by night and travels by day, he said: “Amir ibn al-Tufayl and Arbad ibn Rabi’ah came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Amir said: What will you give me if I follow you? He said: You are a knight, I will give you the reins of the horses. He said: No. He said: What do you seek? He said: The east is mine and the west is yours. He said: No. He said: The wool is mine and the cloak is yours. He said: No. He said: Then I will fill it for you with horses and men. He said: May God protect you from that and the sons of Qaylah,” meaning the Aws and the Khazraj. He said: So they went out, and Amir said to Arbad: If the man is ours, he is well-protected. If we killed him, two goats would not butt heads over him, and they would be satisfied with us giving him a trophy for them, and they loved peace and hated war when they saw something happening. The other said: If you wish. So they consulted each other, and he said: Go back and I will distract him from you by arguing, and be behind him and strike him with the sword once. So they were like that: one behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the other said: Tell us your story. He said: What do you say? He said: Your Quran! So he began to argue with him and to delay him, until he said: What is the matter with you, you are shy? He said: I put my hand on the hilt of my sword and it dried up, so I was not able to undo it or command it or move it. He said: So they went out, and when they were in Al-Harrah, Sa`d bin Mu`adh and Usayd bin Hudayr heard about that, so they went out to them, each of them carrying his slave girl, and his spear in his hand, and he was wearing his sword. They said to `Amir bin At-Tufayl: O one-eyed, O Ablakh, are you the one who imposes conditions on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? If you were not under the protection of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, you would not have thrown yourself at the house until we struck your neck, but do not help. The most severe of the two men against him was Usayd bin Hudayr, so he said: Who is this? They said: Asid bin Hudhair! He said: If his father were alive, he would not have done this to me! Then he said to Arbad: You go out, Arbad, to the region of Adenah, and I will go out to Najd, so we can gather the men and meet him. So Arbad went out until he was in Ar-Raqm, God sent a summer cloud with lightning in it and burned him. He said: And Aamer went out until he was in a valley called Al-Jarir, God sent the plague upon him, and he began to cry: O family of Aamer, a morning like the morning of a virgin is killing me! O family of Aamer, a morning like the morning of a virgin is killing me, and death also in the house of Saluliya! She is a woman from Qais. That is the saying of God: Whether you conceal your speech or declare it aloud, and he recited until he reached: They guard it, those are the successors from the command of God, this is the first and the last, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there are successors who guard him from before him and from behind him, those are the successors from the command of God. And he said to these two: Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves, and he recited until he reached: And He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills, the verse, and he recited until he reached: And the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error. He said: And Labid said about his brother Arbad while he was crying over him: I fear death for Arbad, but I do not fear the star of the fish or the lion Thunder and lightning struck me with the knight on the day of the calamity of Najd Abu Jaafar said: This statement that Ibn Zayd said in interpreting this verse is a statement far from the interpretation of the verse, and it contradicts the statements of those we mentioned from the people of interpretation. This is because he made the ha’ in his statement, For him are successors, from the mention of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was not mentioned in the verse before it or in the one before the other, unless he wanted to return it to his statement, You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, “For him are successors.” If that is the case, then that is far-fetched, with the verses between them without mentioning the report about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If that is the case, then it is closer to the word who in his statement, and whoever is belittled by night, because it is before it and the report is after it. If that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement is: It is the same among you, O people, whether you keep your speech secret or declare it openly before your Lord, whether you are a man who belittles his immorality and suspicion in the darkness of the night, or a wanderer who goes and comes in the light of day, protected by his soldiers and guards who pursue him from among the people of God’s obedience, so that they may prevent him from what he is doing, and that they may establish God’s punishment upon him. That is His statement: They protect him by the command of God. And His statement: Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves, the Most High says: Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people, of well-being and blessings, so He removes that from them and destroys them, until they change what is in themselves, of that, by oppressing one another and transgressing against one another, so then His punishment and change will befall them. And His statement: And when God intends evil for a people, there is none that can avert it, meaning: And if God intends, for these people who hide by night and sneak by day, who have soldiers and protection before them and behind them to protect them from God’s command, destruction and disgrace in this worldly life, there is none that can avert it, meaning: No one is able to avert that from them except God. God the Most High says: And they have no protector besides Him, meaning: And these people, and the ha’ and the mim in for Him, are from the mention of the people in His statement: And when God intends evil for a people, besides God, no protector, meaning: a protector who follows them and takes care of their affairs and punishment. Some scholars of Arabic language used to say: Evil means destruction. They also say: Every leprosy, vitiligo, blindness, and great affliction is evil, with the first letter being a damma. If the first letter is a fatha, it is a verbal noun: I became evil. From this comes their saying: A bad man. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of his saying: And he who is ignorant of the night and travels during the day. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of his saying: And whoever is hidden at night, and whoever is apparent at night, is from their saying: I concealed the thing, if I revealed it, and as Imru’ al-Qais said: If you conceal the disease, we will not fear it, and if you start a war, we will not sit back. He said: It was read I almost hid it, meaning: I revealed it. He said in his statement: And a thief during the day, the thief is the one who hides, as if he directed him to the fact that he became hidden in the threshing floor during the day. Some grammarians of Basra and Kufa said: The meaning of this is: And whoever is hidden, that is, concealed at night, from concealment, and saribb by day, and going by day, from their saying: the camels saribbat to graze, which is their going to the pastures and going out to them. It was said that the nightingale is in the evening, and the morning is in the morning. They also differed on the feminization of Mu’aqabat, which is an attribute of non-females. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It was made feminine because of the frequency of that, such as: genealogist and scholar, then it was made masculine because the meaning is masculine, so he said: they preserve it. Some grammarians of Kufa said: It is: angels who follow one another, then it was made plural followers, so it is a plural of a plural, then it was said: they preserve it. We have already mentioned the meaning of: the one who hides at night and the one who travels during the day. As for what we mentioned about the Basran grammarians in this regard, it is a statement, even if it has a basis in the speech of the Arabs, that contradicts the statement of the people of interpretation. And it is sufficient evidence of its corruption that it departs from the statement of all of them. As for: the ones that follow, then following, in the speech of the Arabs, is the return after the beginning, and the return to something after turning away from it, from the saying of God Almighty: He turned back and did not return, meaning: He did not return, and as Salamah bin Jandal said: And we made the horses follow in their footsteps, returning like hooves from the beginning and the end. Meaning: In a second invasion, they followed, as Tarafa said: I was blaming you, but you followed with sins that were not forgiven. He means by his saying: you have returned. And it has been given the feminine gender in our view, and it is from the description of the guards who guard the one who hides at night and the one who travels during the day, because it was meant to guard the one who follows, then the one who follows was made plural and it was said Mu’aqabat, so that is the plural of the plural of Mu’aqab, and Mu’aqab is the singular of Mu’aqaba, as Labid said: Until he leaves in the souls, and the one who seeks his oppressed right is agitated by the pursuit of his right And the followers, plural. Then he said: They memorize it, so he returned the report to the reminder of the guards and soldiers. As for his saying: They protect it from the command of God, the Arab scholars differed about its meaning. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Its meaning is: He has consequences from the command of God that they preserve, and it is not from His command that they preserve, rather it is an advancement and a delay. He said: And they preserve it with that preservation from the command of God and with His permission, just as you say to a man: I answered you from your supplication to Me, and with your supplication to Me. Some Basran grammarians said that the meaning of this is: They protect it from God’s command, just as they said: He fed me from hunger and from hunger, and He clothed me from nakedness and from nakedness. We have previously demonstrated that the most correct interpretation of this is that His statement, They guard him by the command of God, is a description of the guards of this hidden person at night, and she guards him thinking that she is protecting him from the command of God. So God, the Most High, informed us that this guard will not avail him at all if His command comes, so He said, And when God intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector besides Him.
13:12: God Almighty says: It is He who shows you lightning, causing fear and hope, and produces the heavy clouds.
13:13: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: It is He who shows you the lightning, meaning that the Lord is the One who shows His servants the lightning, and His saying: He is a metaphor for His name, may His praise be glorified. We have explained the meaning of lightning and mentioned the differences of opinion among the interpreters of the word, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And his saying: fear, he says: fear for the traveler from his harm. And that is because lightning, the water, in this place is like: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, he said, Musa bin Salim Abu Jahdam, the client of Ibn Abbas, told us: Ibn Abbas wrote to Abu al-Jild asking him about lightning, and he said: Lightning is water. And his saying: And out of hope, he says: And out of hope for the resident that it will rain and he will benefit, like: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Aqatada, regarding his statement: It is He who shows you lightning, causing fear and hope, meaning: fear for the traveler on his journeys, fearing its harm and hardship, and hope, for the resident, hoping for its blessing and benefit, and hoping for God’s provision. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Fear and hope, fear for the traveler, and hope for the resident. And His saying: And He creates the heavy clouds, and He stirs up the heavy clouds with rain and initiates it. It is said: God created the clouds, if He started them. And the clouds originated, if they began, originates, originated. And the clouds in this place, even if it is in one word, it is a plural, its singular is cloud, and that is why he said: the heavy ones, so he described it with a plural description. If the heavy cloud had come, it would have been permissible, and it would have been a unification of the word cloud, as it was said: Who made for you from the green tree fire. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And He creates the heavy clouds, he said: those in which there is water. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And He creates the heavy clouds, he said: those in which there is water. And His saying: And the thunder glorifies Him with praise. Abu Jaafar said: We have explained the meaning of thunder previously, so there is no need to repeat it here. It was mentioned that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard the sound of thunder, he would say, as follows: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Kathir bin Hisham told us, Jaafar told us: “It has reached us that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard the sound of severe thunder, he would say: O God, do not kill us with Your wrath, do not destroy us with Your punishment, and pardon us before that.” Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who traced the hadith back to the Prophet: “When he heard thunder, he would say: Glory be to He whom the thunder glorifies with His praise.” Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Mas`adah bin Al-Yas` Al-Bahili told us, on the authority of Ja`far bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: “Whenever he heard the sound of thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him Whom it glorifies.” He said, Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Aban, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “When he heard thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him whom it glorifies.” Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ya`la bin Al-Harith told us, I heard Abu Sakhra narrating on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Yazid: “When he heard thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him Whom it glorifies, or: Glory be to Him Whom the thunder glorifies with His praise and the angels out of fear of Him.” He said, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, and Abd al-Karim, on the authority of Tawus: “When he heard thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him whom it glorifies.” Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Maysarah, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, who said: Ibn Abi Zakariya used to say: Whoever says when he hears thunder: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, no lightning will strike him. The meaning of his saying: And the thunder glorifies Him with praise, is that God magnifies and glorifies the thunder, praising Him with His attributes, and denouncing what the polytheists attributed to Him, and what they described Him with, such as taking a companion and a son. Exalted is our Lord and sanctified. And his saying: Out of fear of Him, means: And the angels glorify Him out of fear of God and His awe. As for his saying: And He sends down thunderbolts and strikes with them whomever He wills. We have previously explained the meaning of thunderbolt, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it, with sufficient evidence, and we mentioned what is in it from the narration. There is a difference of opinion about who this verse was revealed to. Some of them said: It was revealed about an infidel among the infidels who mentioned God Almighty and glorified Him in a way other than that in which He should be mentioned, so a thunderbolt was sent upon him that destroyed him. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated, Affan narrated, Abaan bin Yazid narrated, Abu Imran Al-Joni narrated, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Sahar Al-Abdi: It reached him that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to a tyrant and called him, saying: Have you seen your Lord? Is He gold, or silver, or pearls? He said: While he was arguing with them, God sent a cloud that thundered, so God sent a thunderbolt upon him that took the top of his head, so God revealed this verse: And He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills while they dispute about God, and He is severe in penalty. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: A Jew came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Tell me about your Lord, what is He made of? Pearls or rubies? Then a thunderbolt came and took him, and God revealed: And He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills while they dispute about God, and He is severe in penalty. Others said: It was revealed about a disbeliever who denied the Qur’an and called the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a liar. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that a man denied the Qur’an and lied about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God sent a thunderbolt upon him and destroyed him, and God Almighty revealed about him: And they dispute about God, while He is severe in penalty. Others said: It was revealed about Arbad, the brother of Labid bin Rabi’ah, and he and Amer bin Tufail intended to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: The verse, And He sends down thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills was revealed about Labid bin Rabi’ah, because Arbad and Amir bin Tufail bin Malik bin Ja’far came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Amir said: O Muhammad, shall I submit and be the caliph after you? He said: No! He said: So I will be in charge of the people of the hair, and you in charge of the people of the mud? He said: No! He said: What is that? He said: I will give you the reins of the horses to fight on, for you are a knight. He said: Are the reins of the horses not in my hand? By God, I will fill them against you with horses and men from Banu Amir! He said to Arbad: Either you suffice him for me and I will strike him with the sword, or I will suffice him for you and you will strike him with the sword. Arbad said: I will suffice him and strike him. Ibn Tufail said: O Muhammad, I have a need of you. He said: Come closer! He kept coming closer and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Come closer, until he placed his hands on his knees and bent over him, and Arbad drew the sword, and drew a little of it, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw its gleam, he sought refuge in a verse that he used to seek refuge in, and Arbad’s hand on the sword dried up, so God sent a thunderbolt upon him and burned him, and that is what his brother said: I fear death for Irbid, but I do not fear the star of the fish and the lion Lightning and thunderbolts struck me with the knight on the day of the calamity of Najd I mentioned before the story of Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid in a similar manner to this story. And his saying: And they dispute about God, he says: And these are the ones whom God struck with thunderbolts, He struck them with them while they were disputing about God Almighty with His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His saying: And He is severe in penalty, God Almighty says: And God is severe in His penalty in punishing whoever transgresses against Him, is rebellious, and persists in his disbelief. The word mahal is derived from the saying of the speaker: I did not harass so-and-so, so I will harass him with harassment and harassment. It is derived from the verb mahalt I harassed someone, when a man exposes a man to something that will destroy him. From this comes his saying: And the truthful one did not harass him. From this comes the saying of A’sha of Banu Tha’labah: A branch of a spring shakes in the branch of glory, abundant in dew, very difficult to obtain. This is how Muammar ibn al-Muthanna used to recite it, as I narrated on the authority of Ali ibn al-Mughira, on his authority. As for the narrators after that, they recite it: Branch by branch, trembling in the branches of glory, abundant in dew and great in impossibility. Muammar bin Al-Muthanna interpreted this, and claimed that he meant punishment, deceit, and humiliation. Another saying is from this: There is no difference between people, for each has his own problems and difficulties prepared for him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, he said, Saif told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: And He is severe in punishment, he said: severe in taking. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid: And He is severe in punishment, he said: severe in strength. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He is severe in penalty, meaning: strength and cunning. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan: Severe in difficulty, meaning destruction. He said: If it is difficult, then it is severe. Qatada said: Severe in resourcefulness. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, a man told us, on the authority of Ikrimah: And they dispute about God, and He is severe in penalty, he said: The dispute of Arbad, And He is severe in penalty, he said: What struck Arbad of lightning. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And He is severe in punishment, he said, Ibn Abbas said: severe in strength. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And He is severe in penalty, he said: severe in strength, penalty, strength. Abu Ja`far said: The statement that we mentioned from Qatada in the interpretation of al-mahal is that it is a trick, and the statement that Ibn Jurayj mentioned from Ibn Abbas indicate that they used to recite and it is very difficult, with the opening of the m, because the source of the trick does not come as mahalan, with the breaking of the m, but it may come in the estimation of the muf’al from it, so it is mahalah, and from that is their saying: A person is inevitably unable, and mahalah in this place is the muf’al from haylah, but as for with the breaking of the m, it is only a source from mahalat fulan amahaluhu mahalan, and mumalahah is far in meaning from haylah. Abu Jaafar said: I do not know of anyone who read it with the opening of the meem. If that is the case, then what is more deserving of its interpretation is what we have said.
13:14: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: God has created the true call, and the call is the truth, just as the abode was added to the hereafter in His statement: And for the home of the hereafter. We have explained that previously. What he meant by the true call was the oneness of God and the testimony that there is no god but God. And in a similar manner to what we said, the people of interpretation interpreted it. Who said that? Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The call to truth, he said: There is no god but God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: His is the call of truth, he said: The testimony that there is no god but God. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, Saif told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: His is the call to truth, he said: monotheism. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: His statement: His is the call of truth, he said: There is no god but God. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said regarding his statement: His is the call of truth, he said: There is no god but God. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, His is the true call, there is no god but God. It is not appropriate for anyone other than Him. It is not appropriate to say: So-and-so is the god of the sons of so-and-so. And His statement: And those they call upon besides Him, God Almighty says: And the gods that the polytheists call upon as lords and gods. And his saying: Beyond Him, means: besides God. What he meant by his saying: besides Him is the gods, that they are inferior to Him, and that they cannot be a god, and it is not permissible for there to be a god except the One, All-Powerful God, and from this is the saying of the poet: Are you threatening me behind Bani Riyah? You lied, your hands will fall short against me. It means: Your hands will fall short on me. And His statement: They do not respond to them with anything, meaning: These gods, whom these polytheists call upon as gods, do not respond to anything they want of benefit or warding off harm, except like one who extends his hands toward the water, meaning: The supplication of the one who calls upon the gods does not benefit him from his supplication to them, except as the supplication of the one who extends his hands toward the water benefits him by extending them toward it without raising it to it in a vessel, but rather so that it rises to it by his supplication to it, his pointing to it, and his grasping it. The Arabs use an example of someone who strives for something he cannot attain, like someone who holds onto water. Some of them said: I and you are longing for you like someone who holds water but his fingers have not given him water. He means by that: He has nothing in his hand of that except what is in the hand of one who holds water, because one who holds water has nothing in his hand. Another said: So, because of the love that was between us, I became like someone holding water in his hand. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Saif told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement: Except like one who stretches out his hands toward water to reach his mouth, but he cannot reach it, he said: Like a thirsty man who stretches out his hand to the well so that the water can rise to him, but he cannot reach it. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his saying: Like one who extends his hands toward the water, he calls for the water with his tongue, and points to it with his hand, but it never comes to it. He said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Al-A’raj told me, on the authority of Mujahid: Let his mouth reach it, he calls him to come to him, but he will not come to him. Likewise, he who is below him does not respond. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Like one who extends his hands toward the water, calling for water with his tongue, and pointing to it with his hand, but it never comes to him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid. He said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, like the hadith of Al-Hasan Ibn Hajjaj. Ibn Jurayj said: Al-A’raj said, on the authority of Mujahid: Let it reach his mouth, he said: He calls upon Him to come to him, but He will not come to him, so likewise He will not respond to anyone but Him. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: And those they call upon besides Him - they do not respond to them with anything except like one who stretches out his hands toward water to reach his mouth, but it will not reach it, and it will not reach it until his neck is torn apart and he dies of thirst. God the Most High said: And the invocation of the disbelievers is not but in error, this is an example that God has given. That is, this one who calls upon besides this idol and this stone - they will never respond to him with anything, nor will they bring him any good, nor will they ward off any evil from him until death comes to him, like the one who stretches out his arms toward the water to reach his mouth, but it does not reach his mouth, nor will it reach him until he dies of thirst. Others said: The meaning of this is: And those they call upon besides Him do not respond to them at all except like one who extends his hands toward the water, to include his imagination in it, and it is not far-fetched. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Like one who extends his hands toward water to reach his mouth, he said: This is the example of the one who associates others with God, so his example is like the example of the thirsty man who looks at his shadow in the water from afar, and he wants to take it but is unable to. Others said about this: Muhammad bin Saad narrated to me, he said, my father narrated to me, he said, my uncle narrated to me, he said, my father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And those they call upon besides Him - they will not respond to them at all to And the call of the disbelievers is not but in error, he says: The example of the idols and those who worship them besides God is like the example of a man who has been overcome by thirst until death has made him suffocate, and his palms have been placed in the water but they do not reach his mouth. God says: The gods will not respond to nor benefit those who worship them until this man’s palms reach his mouth, and they will never reach his mouth. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And those they invoke besides Him - they do not respond to them at all except as one who extends his hands toward water to reach his mouth, but it will not reach it, he said: They do not benefit them at all except as this one benefits with his hands, meaning extending them to something that he will never reach. Others said about this: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Except like one who extends his hands toward water that it may reach his mouth, and the water will not reach his mouth, as long as he extends his hands and does not close them, “and it will not reach it. And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error,” he said: This is a parable given to the one who takes someone other than God as a god, that it will not benefit him, and will not ward off evil from him, until he dies in that state. And His statement: And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error, meaning: And the supplication of one who disbelieves in God, what he supplicates to of idols and gods, is only in error, meaning: except without rectitude or guidance, because he associates partners with God.
13:15: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: If those who call upon idols and statues as partners for God, other than God, refrain from singling out obedience and sincerity in worship to Him, then to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens of the noble angels, and whoever is on the earth of the believers in Him willingly. As for the disbelievers in Him, they prostrate to Him reluctantly when they are forced to prostrate, as: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion. As for the believer, he prostrates willingly, and as for the disbeliever, he prostrates by compulsion. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: When Rabi’ bin Khaitham recited this verse: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, he said: Yes, my Lord. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, he said: Whoever entered willingly, this is willingly, and by compulsion, is whoever entered only with the sword. And His statement: And their shadows in the mornings and the evenings, means: The shadows of everyone who prostrates willingly or unwillingly also prostrate in the mornings and evenings. This is because the shadow of every person will be shaded in the evening, as the Most High said: Have they not seen what God has created of things? Their shadows extend to the right and the left, prostrating to God, while they are humbled. A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And their shadows in the mornings and the evenings, meaning: when the shadow of one of them falls to his right or his left. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: In the interpretation of Mujahid: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and so do their shadows in the mornings and the evenings, he said: The shadow of the believer prostrates willingly and obediently, and the shadow of the disbeliever prostrates willingly and by compulsion. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And their shadows in the mornings and the evenings, he said: He mentioned that the shadows of all things prostrate to Him, and he recited: Prostrating to God, and they are humbled. He said: Those shadows prostrate to God. Asal is the plural of Asl, and Asl is the plural of Asil. Asil is the evening, which is the period between Asr and sunset. Abu Dhu’ayb said: By my life, you are the home whose people are most honored, and I sit in its shade in the evenings. Say in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?” Say: God. Say: Have you taken besides Him protectors who possess neither benefit nor harm for themselves? Abu Ja`far said: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and their Manager? They will say: God. God commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him) to say: God. So He said to him: Say, O Muhammad, their Lord who created them and brought them into being. He is the One to whom worship is not appropriate except, and He is God. Then He said: If they answer you with that. Then He said to them: Have you taken besides the Lord of the heavens and the earth protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit that they can bring to themselves, nor any harm that they can ward off from themselves? And since they do not possess that for themselves, then whoever possesses it for others is further away. So you worshipped them and abandoned the worship of the One in whose hand is benefit and harm, life and death, and the management of all things. Then He, the Most High, gave them an example and said: “Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?”
13:16: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who worshipped besides God, in whose hand is their benefit and harm, that which neither benefits nor harms: Is the blind equal, who does not see anything and is not guided to the path to follow except by being guided, and the seeing one, who guides the blind person to the path of the road which he does not see? There is no doubt that they are not equal. He says: Likewise, the believer who sees the truth and follows it and knows the guidance and follows it is not equal, and you, O polytheists, do not know the truth and do not see the right path. And His statement: Or are darkness and light equal? God Almighty says: Are darknesses equal in which the path cannot be seen so that one may follow it, and the road cannot be seen so that one may ride it, and the light by which things are seen and whose light dispels the darkness equal? He says: These two are undoubtedly not equal, so is disbelief in God, its owner is in confusion and is always in a state of confusion, from which he does not return to the truth. Belief in God, its owner is in light, acting with knowledge of his Lord, and knowing that he has a rewarder who rewards him for his good deeds, and a punisher who punishes him for his evil deeds, and a provider who provides for him, and a benefactor who benefits him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: “Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are darkness and light equal?” As for the blind and the seeing, they are the disbeliever and the believer, and as for darkness and light, they are guidance and misguidance. And His statement: Or have they attributed to God partners who created like His creation so that the creation became indistinguishable to them? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: Did your idols which you have taken as allies besides God create a creation like God’s creation, so that their matter became unclear to you in what they created and God created, so that you attributed them to Him as partners because of that? Or is it only ignorance and deviation from the right path that you are faced with? It is not difficult for a rational person to believe that worshipping something that does not harm or benefit is ignorance, and that worship is only suitable for the one whose benefit is hoped for and whose harm is feared, just as that is not problematic due to its error or the ignorance of its doer. Likewise, the ignorance of the one who associates in the worship of the One who provides for him, burdens him, and provides for him, the One who has no power to harm or benefit him, is not problematic. Some of the interpreters said something similar to what we said about this. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Or have they attributed to God partners who created like His creation? This led them to doubt the idols. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Or have they attributed to God partners who created like His creation so that the creation became indistinguishable to them? They created like His creation, so that led them to doubt the idols. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Kathir said: I heard Mujahid say: Or have they attributed to God partners who created like His creation so that the creation became indistinguishable to them? I gave an example. And His saying: “Say: God is the Creator of all things,” the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to these polytheists if they acknowledge to you that their idols which they associated with Him in the worship of God do not create anything: God is your Creator and the Creator of your idols and the Creator of all things, so what is the reason for your associating with Him that which does not create and does not harm? And His saying: And He is the One, the Subduer, means: He is the One who has no second, the Subduer, who deserves divinity and worship, not idols and statues that neither harm nor benefit.
13:17: Abu Jaafar said: This is a parable that God gave for truth and falsehood, belief in it and disbelief. God Almighty says: The example of truth in its stability and falsehood in its decay is like that of water that God sent down from the sky to the earth. Then the valleys flowed according to their capacity, meaning: the valleys filled it with it, the large in its largeness and the small in its smallness. Then the torrent carried a rising foam, meaning: the torrent that resulted from that water that God sent down from the sky carried a rising foam above the torrent. This is one of the two parables of truth and falsehood. Truth is the remaining water that God sent down from the sky, and the foam that is of no use is falsehood. Another example: And from what they kindle in the fire, seeking adornment, God Almighty says: Another example of truth and falsehood is like silver or gold that people kindle in the fire seeking adornment to make or goods, and that is from copper, lead, and iron, it is kindled to make goods from it that are beneficial, froth like it, God Almighty says: And from what they kindle from these things is foam like it, meaning: like the foam of a torrent, it is of no benefit and goes away in vain, just as one does not benefit from the foam of a torrent and goes away in vain. And he raised the foam by saying: And from what they kindle in the fire. The meaning of the words: And from what they kindle in the fire is foam like the foam of a torrent in the length of its foam, and the remaining pure gold and silver. God the Almighty says: Thus does God set forth the truth and falsehood, meaning: just as God sets forth the parable of faith and disbelief, in the length of disbelief and the disappointment of its owner when God rewards him with the remaining beneficial water of the flood and pure gold and silver, so does God set forth the truth and falsehood, As for the foam, it vanishes as scum, meaning: as for the foam that rises above the flood and the gold, silver, copper and lead when the fuel is poured over it, it vanishes due to the winds blowing it and the water throwing it, and it clings to the trees and sides of the valley. As for what benefits people from water, gold, silver, lead and copper, the water remains in the earth so it drinks it, and the gold and silver remain for people. Thus does God set forth parables, meaning: just as He sets forth this parable of faith and disbelief, so does He set forth parables. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity, this is a parable that God has set, and hearts can bear it according to the extent of their certainty and doubt. As for doubt, deeds do not benefit from it, but as for certainty, God benefits its people with it, and it is His statement: As for the foam, it vanishes as scum, which is doubt, But that which benefits people remains on the earth, which is certainty, just as jewelry is placed in the fire, and its pure part is taken and its impurity is left in the fire. So too does God accept certainty and leave doubt. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their capacity, and the flood carries away a swelling foam, meaning: The flood carries away what is in the valley of wood and dung, and from that which they heat in the fire, which is gold, silver, ornaments, goods, copper and iron. Copper and iron have impurities, so God made their impurities like the foam of water. As for that which benefits people, it is gold and silver. As for that which benefits the earth, it is what it drinks of the water and produces. So He made that like a righteous deed that remains for its people, and the deed is something that vanishes from its people, just as this foam vanishes. So guidance and truth come from God, so whoever acts according to the truth, it will be for him, and it will remain just as that which benefits people on earth remains. And similarly, iron cannot be made into a knife or a sword until it is put into the fire, which consumes its impurities, and its goodness comes out and is used. Thus, falsehood will vanish on the Day of Resurrection, when people will be raised up and deeds will be presented. Falsehood will be lost and destroyed, and the people of truth will benefit from the truth. Then He said: And from that which they kindle in the Fire in search of adornment or goods is a foam like it. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow, to a provision of foam like it, he said: Seeking adornments of gold and silver, or provisions of brass and iron. He said: Just as gold, silver, brass and iron are kindled and their essence is extracted. He said: “Thus does God compare truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes as scum, but that which benefits people remains on the earth,” thus the truth remains for its people, so they benefit from it. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Za'farani narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj bin Muhammad narrated to us, he said, Ibn Jurayj said, Abdullah bin Kathir informed me: that he heard Mujahid say: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity, he said: they could not bear to fill them, and the flood carries a swelling foam, he said: the speech ended. Then he turned to the next step and said: And from that which they heat in the fire in search of adornment or goods is a foam like it, he said: the goods are iron, copper, lead and the like, a foam like it, he said: the dross of that is like the foam of a flood. He said: But as for that which benefits people, it remains in the earth, "as for the foam, it vanishes as scum," he said: that is the example of truth and falsehood. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Kathir, on the authority of Mujahid: that he heard him say, and he mentioned something similar, and added to it, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said, his statement: But as for the foam, it vanishes as scum, he said: solidified in the earth, But that which benefits people remains in the earth, meaning water. And they are two examples, like truth and falsehood. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: a rising foam, meaning a torrent, like the dross of iron and ornaments, then it vanishes, solidified in the ground, and from that which they heat in the fire in search of ornaments or goods is a foam like it, meaning iron, copper, lead and the like. And his statement: but as for that which benefits people, it remains on the earth, these are two examples of truth and falsehood. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid. He said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid - one of them adds more than the other - regarding his statement: And the valleys flow according to their capacity, he said: similar to it, and the torrent carries a swelling foam, he said: the foam is the torrent, in search of ornaments or goods, a foam like it, he said: the dross of iron and the ornament, but as for the foam, it vanishes, he said: solidified in the earth, but as for that which benefits people, it remains in the earth, he said: water. And they are two examples of truth and falsehood. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their capacity, the small according to its smallness, and the large according to its largeness, and the torrent carries a swelling foam, meaning high, “and from that which they heat in the fire in search of adornment or goods is a foam like it. Thus does God present the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes as scum,” and scum is what clings to trees, but that which benefits people remains on the earth. These are three examples that God presented in one example. He says: Just as this foam vanishes and becomes scum that is of no benefit and whose blessing is not given, so falsehood vanishes from its people just as falsehood vanishes from its people just as this foam vanishes, and just as this water remained in the earth, so this earth sprouted and brought forth its plants, so the truth remains for its people just as this water remained in the earth and God brought forth with it what it brought forth of plants. His statement: And from that which they kindle in the fire, the verse, just as pure gold and silver remain when it is put into the fire and its impurities are gone, so the truth remains for its people. His statement, Or a foam-like provision, he says: This iron and brass that is used has benefits. He says: Just as the pure of this iron and brass remains when it is put into the fire and its impurities are gone, so the truth remains for its people just as their pure remains. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: "And the valleys flow according to their capacity, the large according to its capacity, and the small according to its capacity, as a swelling foam," he said: The foam rose above the water, "and from that which they heat in the fire," he said: It is gold, when it is put into the fire, its pure part remains and what was of its turbidity is removed. This is a parable that God has given for truth and falsehood, "As for the foam, it vanishes as scum," it clings to the tree and becomes nothing. This is a parable of falsehood, "As for that which benefits people, it remains in the earth," this produces plants. It is a parable of truth, "Or provision of foam like it," he said: The provision is brass and iron. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated, Hudha bin Khalifa narrated, Awf narrated, saying: It reached me regarding His statement, He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their capacity, that God has set forth this for truth and falsehood, and valleys flow according to their capacity, the small according to its capacity, the large according to its capacity, and what is in between according to its capacity, and the torrent carries a swelling foam, meaning enormous, and wherever the water settles, the foam disappears as scum and the wind blows it away and it becomes nothing, and what remains is pure water that benefits people, from it their drink, their plants, and their benefit, or a provision of foam like it, and foam is like everything that is lit in fire, gold, silver, copper, and iron, so its impurity disappears and what is beneficial remains in their hands. And impurity and foam are like falsehood, and what benefits people from what they obtain in their hands that benefits them is money, which is in their hands. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And from that which they kindle in the fire in pursuit of adornment or goods is a foam like it, he said: This is a parable that God has given for truth and falsehood. So he recited, He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their capacity, and the torrent carries a swelling foam, this foam is of no benefit, or goods of foam like it, this is of no benefit either. He said: And the water remained on the earth and benefited the people, and the ornaments that were made from this remained and the people benefited from it, “But as for the foam, it vanishes as cast-off, but that which benefits the people remains on the earth. Thus God presents examples,” and he said: This is a parable that God has given for truth and falsehood. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said: Valleys according to their size, meaning the small according to its smallness, and the large according to its largeness. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Talha bin Amr told us, on the authority of Ata’: God gave an example of truth and falsehood. He gave an example of truth as a flood that remains on the earth, and He gave an example of falsehood as the foam that does not benefit people. He meant by his saying: Rabia, high and swollen, from their saying: The thing raaba yarbawan grows, so it is raab raab. From this, the elevated part of the earth, like a hill, is called rabia a hill. From this, God Almighty said: It shook and swelled. Copper, lead, and iron are called goods in this context, because they are enjoyed, and everything that people enjoy is good, as the poet said: Enjoy, you disheveled one, for the only thing that precedes death is enjoyment. As for rudeness, I: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah Muammar ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: It is said: The pot has boiled over, meaning when it boils and its foam pours out, or it becomes still and nothing remains of it. Some Arabists from Basra claimed that the meaning of his saying: It goes away scum is that the earth dries it up. He said: It is said: The valley became scum and Ajfa meaning to dry up, and The valley became scum if it brought that scum. And The valley became scum means to scum and to scum and it was mentioned about the Arabs that they say: I drank the pot, I drank it, if it brought out its scum, which is the foam that rises above it, and I drank it ijfa’a, in a language. He said: They said: I drank the man jaf’a, meaning I defeated him. It was said: "It goes away, it became dry", meaning: it became dry, because it is a source from the saying of the speaker: The valley dried up its scum, so it came out in the manner of a noun, which is a source. This is how the Arabs do with the source of everything that was from an action of something that came together, such as cloth, flour, debris, and scum, they bring it out in the manner of a noun, as they did in their saying I gave him an offering, meaning giving. If the source was intended from cloth, it would have been correct to say: He clothed him with cloth.
13:18: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: As for those who responded to God and believed in Him when He called them to believe in Him, and obeyed and followed His Messenger and believed in what he brought them from God, they will have the best, which is Paradise, likewise: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: For those who responded to their Lord is the best, which is Paradise. And His statement: And those who did not respond to him - if they had all that is in the earth and as much more with it, they would ransom themselves thereby, the Most High says: As for those who did not respond to God when He called them to His Oneness and to acknowledge His Lordship, and did not obey Him in what He commanded them to do, and did not follow His Messenger and believe in what He brought them from their Lord, then if they had all that is in the earth and as much more with it as their property, then He accepted the same from them, and accepted from them instead of the punishment that God has prepared for them in the fire of Hell and as compensation, they would ransom themselves thereby from Him. God says: For those, there is an evil reckoning, meaning: These are those who did not respond to God, for them is an evil reckoning, meaning: For them, with God, He will take them for all their sins, and He will not forgive them anything of them, but He will punish them for all of them, as: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Awn told us, on the authority of Farqad al-Sabkhi, who said, Shahr bin Hawshab told us: Bad accounting means that nothing will be overlooked for them. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Hajjaj bin Abi Uthman told me, he said, Farqad al-Sabkhi told me, he said, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: O Farqad, do you know what evil reckoning is? I said: No! He said: It is that a man is held accountable for all of his sins and nothing of them is forgiven for him. His statement: And their abode is Hell, meaning: Their dwelling place in which they will reside on the Day of Resurrection is Hell. And an evil resting place, meaning: And an evil bed and comforter is Hell, which is their abode on the Day of Resurrection.
13:19: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Is this one who knows that what God has revealed to you, O Muhammad, is true and believes in it, confirms it, and acts according to what is in it, like the one who is blind, who does not know the location of God’s proof upon him, nor does he know what God has obligated him to do of His obligations? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth? He said: These are people who benefited from what they heard from the Book of God and understood it and comprehended it. God said: Like one who is blind, he said: about goodness so he does not see it. His saying: Only those with understanding will remember, means: Only those with intellects will be admonished by the verses of God and will take heed of them, and they are minds, the singular of which is lab.
13:20: God Almighty says: Those who fulfill the covenant of God and do not break the contract.
13:21: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Only those with understanding will take heed and consider the verses of God, who fulfill God’s commandment that He has commanded them, and do not break the covenant, and do not violate the covenant that they have made with God to the contrary, by doing other than what He has commanded them to do, and disobeying what He has forbidden. We have explained the meaning of the covenant and the pact, previously, with its evidence, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Only those of understanding will remember, so he explained who they are, saying: Those who fulfill the covenant of God and do not break the contract, so you must fulfill the covenant and do not break this covenant, for God the Most High has forbidden and presented it with the utmost precedence, so He mentioned it in twenty-some places as advice to you, as an introduction to you, and as an argument against you. And the matter is only magnified by the way God magnified it for the people of understanding and reason, so magnify it as God magnified it. Qatada said: “It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say in his sermon: There is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness, and there is no religion for one who has no covenant.” And His statement: And those who maintain what God has commanded to be maintained, God Almighty says: And those who maintain the ties of kinship which God has commanded them to maintain and do not sever them, and fear their Lord, meaning: And they fear God in severing them, lest they sever them and He punish them for severing them and for disobeying His command concerning them. And His statement: And they fear the evil of the reckoning, means: And they are wary of God discussing them in the reckoning, and then not pardoning them for their sin. So, out of their fear of that, they are serious about obeying Him, preserving His limits, as: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Jaafar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Amr bin Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’ regarding his statement: Those who fear their Lord and dread the evil of reckoning, he said: Comparison by deeds. He said, Affan told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Farqad, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Bad accounting means that someone who will not be forgiven will be held accountable. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And they fear the evil of the reckoning, he said, so he said: What is the evil of the reckoning? He said: That which is not permissible. Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Farqad, he said: Ibrahim said to me: Do you know what evil reckoning is? I said: I do not know. He said: The servant will be held accountable for all of his sins, and nothing of them will be forgiven.
13:22: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And those who are patient in fulfilling the covenant of God, and refraining from breaking the covenant, and maintaining kinship ties, seeking the face of their Lord, and what he means by his saying: seeking the face of their Lord, is seeking to glorify God, and to sanctify Him from disobeying His command, or doing something that He hates to do and thus disobeying Him, and establish prayer, meaning: and perform the obligatory prayer within its limits and at its times, and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, meaning: and pay the obligatory zakat from their wealth and spend from it in the ways in which God has commanded them to spend, secretly, in rudeness, and publicly, in appearance, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And establish prayer, meaning the five daily prayers, and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, meaning: zakat. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: Patience is to remain. He said, and he said: Patience, in these two, so be patient for God’s sake with what He loves even if it is difficult for the souls and bodies, and be patient with what He hates even if desires incline towards it. So whoever is like this is among the patient. And he recited: (Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.)
