And his saying: And they repel evil with good, means: And they repel the harm of those who have harmed them from among the people by doing good to them, as: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And they repel evil with good, he said: They repel evil with good, they do not repay evil with evil, but they repel it with good. And His statement: For them is the final home, God Almighty says: These are the ones whose characteristics We have described, they are the ones for them is the final home, meaning: They are the ones whom God has granted the abode of Paradise in return, instead of their abode which, had they not been believers, would have been in the Fire, so God has granted them this in return from that. It has been said: The meaning of this is: Those will have, after their obedience to their Lord in this world, the abode of Paradise.
13:23: God Almighty says: “Gardens of Eden, which they will enter, as will those who were righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate.”
13:24: Abu Jaafar said: He says: Gardens of Eden, a translation of the afterlife, just as it is said: What a good man Abdullah is, so Abdullah is the man to whom it is said: What a good man. The interpretation of the words: Those will have, after their obedience to their Lord, the home which is the Gardens of Eden. We have explained the meaning of his saying: Aden, and that it means a residence with no stabbing. And His statement: And those who were righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring, the Most High says: Gardens of Eden will be entered by those whose characteristics He has described, and they are those who fulfill the covenant of God, and those who join what God has commanded to be joined, and fear their Lord, and those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer, and do the actions that the Most High mentioned in these three verses, and those who were righteous among their fathers, their spouses, which are their women and families, and their offspring. Their righteousness, their faith in God, and their following of His command and the command of His Messenger, peace be upon him, as: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And those among their fathers who were righteous, he said: Those who believed in this world. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid -: And Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And those among their fathers who were righteous, he said: those among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring who believed. And His statement: “And the angels will enter upon them from every gate. Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured.” God Almighty says: And the angels will enter upon those whom God Almighty described in these three verses, in the Gardens of Eden, from every gate of them, saying to them: “Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured,” in obeying your Lord in this world. And excellent is the final home. He mentioned that the Aden Gardens have five thousand gates. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ali bin Jarir told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ya`la bin Ata`, on the authority of Nafi` bin Asim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: In Paradise there is a palace called Aden, surrounded by towers and meadows, in it are five thousand doors, on each door are five thousand inkwells, none will enter it except a prophet, a friend, or a martyr. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Gardens of Eden, he said: The city of Paradise, in which are the messengers, prophets, martyrs, and imams of guidance, and the people around them are equal in number to the number of gardens around it. And he omitted from his statement: “And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, ‘Peace be upon you,’” they say, as the indication of the speech was sufficient for it, just as he omitted that from his statement: And if you could but see when the criminals will lower their heads before their Lord, ‘Our Lord, we have seen.’ Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Baqiyyah ibn Al-Walid, who said, Arta’ah ibn Al-Mundhir told me: I heard a man from the elders of the army called Abu Al-Hajjaj say: I sat with Abu Umamah and he said: When a believer enters Paradise, he will be reclining on his couch, and with him are two rows of servants, and at the edge of the rows is a gated door. An angel will come forward asking permission, and the servant closest to him will say to the one next to him: An angel is asking permission! And the one next to him will say to the one next to him: An angel is asking permission, until he reaches the believer and he says: Give permission. So the one closest to the believer will say: Give permission. And the one next to him will say to the one next to him: Give permission. And so on until he reaches the one closest to the believer, who is at the door, and it is opened for him, so he enters and greets him, then leaves. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Salih, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to visit the graves of the martyrs at the beginning of each year and say: “Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. What an excellent final home!” And Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman. As for his saying: “Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured,” the people of interpretation said about that something similar to what we said about it. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Imran al-Joni: that he recited this verse: “Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured,” he said: for your religion. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, “Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured,” he said: When they were patient with what God loves and presented it. And he recited: He will reward them for what they patiently endured with a garden and silk garments, until he reached: And your effort is ever appreciated, and they were patient with what God disliked and prohibited for them, and they were patient with what was difficult for them and God loved, so He greeted them with that. And he recited: (And the angels will enter upon them from every gate. Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.) As for his saying: Then excellent is the final home, its meaning is, God willing, as… Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Abu Imran al-Joni, regarding his statement: Then excellent is the final home, he said: Paradise from Hell.
13:25: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: As for those who break the covenant of God, and their breaking it is their disobedience to God’s command, and their actions in disobedience to Him, after their covenant, meaning after they have pledged to God to do what He has entrusted to them, and sever what God has commanded to be joined, meaning they sever the ties of kinship that God has commanded them to join, and cause corruption on the earth, meaning their corruption in it is their actions in it in disobedience to God, for them is the curse, meaning they will be far from His mercy and excluded from His gardens, and for them is the evil home, meaning they will have what will harm them in the Hereafter. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The greatest of the major sins is associating partners with God, because God says: And whoever associates partners with God - it is as if he had fallen from the sky and was beaten by birds, and breaking a covenant, and severing family ties, because God Almighty says: For those is the curse, and for them is the evil home, meaning: the evil end. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, regarding His statement: And they sever that which God has commanded to be joined, he said: “It has reached us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you do not walk to your relative on foot, and do not give him from your wealth, then you have severing ties with him.” Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Mus`ab ibn Sa`d, he said: I asked my father about this verse: Say, ‘Shall We inform you of the greatest losers as to [their] deeds? Those whose effort is lost in worldly life.’ Are they the Kharijites? He said: No, but the Kharijites are: “Those who break the covenant of God after ratifying it and sever that which God has ordered to be joined and spread corruption on earth. Those will have the curse, and they will have the worst home.” So Sa`d used to call them the wicked. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, he said, I heard Mus’ab bin Sa’d say: I was holding the Qur’an for Sa’d, and he came to this verse, then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Muhammad bin Ja’far.
13:26: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: God expands the provision for whomever He wills of His creation, so He expands it for him: because among them there are those for whom nothing but that is good, and He restricts, meaning: He restricts the provision and life of whomever He wills of them, so He makes it difficult for them, because nothing but stinginess is good for them, and they rejoice in the life of this world, God Almighty says: And these people for whom provision was expanded in this world rejoiced, despite their disbelief in God and their disobedience to Him, because of what He expanded for them in it, and they were ignorant of what God has with the people of His obedience and faith in Him in the Hereafter of honor and bliss. Then He, the Most High, informed about the extent of that in this world in what the people of faith in Him will have with Him in the Hereafter, and He informed His servants of its smallness, saying: And the life of this world is not compared to the Hereafter except a temporary enjoyment, meaning: And all that these people were given in this world of abundance, and the provision and comfortable living that was spread out for them in it, in what God has for the people of His obedience in the Hereafter, is only a temporary enjoyment, little and something insignificant and passing away, as: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Except for provisions, he said: A little that is gone. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid. He said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the life of this world is nothing compared to the Hereafter except a passing enjoyment, he said: It is little and fleeting. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Bakir ibn Al-Akhns, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Sabit, regarding his statement: And they rejoice in the life of this world, while the life of this world is not compared to the Hereafter except enjoyment, he said: Like the provisions of the shepherd who provides his family with: a handful of dates, or a little flour, or something to drink milk with.
13:27: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And the polytheists of your people say that, O Muhammad: Why has a sign not been sent down to you from your Lord, either an angel to be with you as a warner, or a treasure thrown down to you? He said: Indeed, God misguides among you whom He wills, O people, and He disappoints him from believing in me and believing in what I have brought him from my Lord, and He guides to Him whoever turns back, so he returns to repentance from his disbelief and belief in Him, and He guides him to follow me and believe in what I have brought him from his Lord. And the misguidance of those among you who go astray is not because a sign has not been sent down to me from my Lord, nor is the guidance of those among you who are guided because it has been sent down to me. Rather, that is in the hand of God. He guides whomever He wills among you to faith, and disappoints whomever He wills among you so that he does not believe. I have explained the meaning of repentance in more than one place in this book of ours with its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And He guides to Him whoever turns back, meaning: whoever repents and turns.
13:28: God Almighty says: “Those who have believed and whose hearts find comfort in the remembrance of God. Unquestionably, in the remembrance of God hearts find comfort.”
13:29: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: And He guides to Himself those who turn back in repentance, those who believe. Those who believed is in the accusative case, in response to whoever, because those who believed are those who repented, which was translated from it. And his saying: And their hearts are reassured by the remembrance of God, means: And their hearts are calmed and comforted by the remembrance of God, as: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “And their hearts find peace in the remembrance of God,” he said: They find peace in the remembrance of God and are comforted by it. And his saying: “Verily, by the remembrance of God do hearts find peace,” means: Verily, by the remembrance of God do the hearts of the believers find peace and comfort. It was said: He meant by that the hearts of the believers among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Verily, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest, referring to Muhammad and his companions. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Verily, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest, he said: for Muhammad and his companions. He said, Ishaq told us, Ahmad bin Yunus told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us regarding his statement: And their hearts find rest in the remembrance of God, he said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His saying: Those who believe and do righteous deeds, righteous deeds, and that is knowledge of what their Lord has commanded them, blessed are they. And blessed is in the nominative case with for them. Some of the people of Basra and Kufa used to say: This is a noun, just as one would say in speech: Woe to Amr. Abu Ja`far said: The nominative case was preferred for tuba because of the beauty of its addition without the letter lam. This is because it is said in it: tubaak, just as it is said: woe to you, and weebeak. If it were not for the beauty of its addition without the letter lam, the accusative case would have been better and more eloquent, just as the accusative case in their saying: Woe to Zayd, “far away from him,” and shame on him, is better, since the addition in it without the letter lam is not beautiful. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying: Blessed are they. Some of them said: It means: Yes, what do they have? Who said that? Jaafar bin Muhammad al-Baruri from the people of Kufa told me, he said, Abu Zakariya al-Kalbi told us, on the authority of Umar bin Nafi’, he said: Ikrimah was asked about Blessings for them, he said: Yes, what is for them. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Omar bin Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: Blessed are they, he said: Yes, what is good for them. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Omar bin Nafi’ told me, he said: I heard Ikrimah regarding his statement: Blessed are they, he said: Yes, what is good for them. Others said: It means: They are blessed. Who said that? Abu Hisham told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak: Blessings to them, he said: Envy for them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, the same. He said, Amr bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, the same. Others said: It means joy and delight. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud and Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, they said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Blessings to them, meaning: joy and delight to the eye. Others said: It means: Good for them. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Blessed are they, meaning: Good for them, and it is a word from the speech of the Arabs. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Blessings to them, this is an Arabic word. A man says: Blessed are you, meaning: you have achieved good. Others said: It means: It is better for them. Who said that? Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: It is better for them. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: Blessed are they, he said: The goodness and dignity that God gave them. Others said: Blessed are they, a name for Paradise, and the meaning of the words is: Paradise is theirs. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Blessed are they, he said: the name of Paradise, in Ethiopian. Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Blessings to them, he said: the name of the land of Paradise, in Abyssinian. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Mashjuj, regarding his statement: Blessed are they, he said: Bliss is the name of Paradise, in Indian. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Dawud bin Mihran told us, he said, Yaqoub told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Mashjuj, he said: The name of Paradise in Hindi is Tuba. Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah: Blessed are they, he said: Paradise. He said, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Blessed are they, he said: Paradise. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is bliss and a good place of return, he said: God did not create Paradise and finish it. He said: Those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is bliss and a good place of return, and that was when he was impressed. Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: Blessed are they, he said: Paradise. Others said: Blessed are they, a tree in Paradise. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Qara bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Musa bin Salim, he said, Ibn Abbas said: Blessings for them is a tree in Paradise. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Ash’ath ibn Abd God, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: Blessed are they, a tree in Paradise, which says to it: Give me whatever my servant wants! So it gives him horses with their saddles and bridles, camels with their reins, and whatever he wants of clothing. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqoub told us, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, he said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, all the trees of Paradise are from it, its branches are behind the wall of Paradise. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Ash’ath bin Abdullah, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: In Paradise there is a tree called Tuba, and God says to it: Tear forth. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Ibn Thawr. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Jabbar told us, he said, Marwan told us, he said, Al-Ala’ told us, on the authority of Shammar bin Atiyah, regarding his statement: Blessings be upon them, he said: It is a tree in Paradise called Tuba. Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hassan Abi al-Ashras, on the authority of Mughith ibn Sami, who said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise. There is no house in Paradise except that there is a branch of it in it. Then a bird comes and perches, and it calls it and eats dried meat from one side and roast meat from the other. Then it says: Fly, and it flies. He said, Abu Saleh told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of some of the people of Ash-Sham, who said: Your Lord took a pearl and placed it in the palms of His hands, then rolled it between His palms, then planted it in the middle of the people of Paradise, then said to it: Stretch until you attain My pleasure. So it did, and when it was straight, the rivers of Paradise gushed forth from its roots, and it is Tuba. Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim Al-San’ani told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me: that he heard Wahb say: In Paradise there is a tree called Tuba, a rider can travel in its shade for a hundred years without crossing it. Its flowers are ryat, its leaves are brocade, its branches are amber, its ground is ruby, its soil is camphor, and its mud is musk. From its roots flow rivers of wine, milk, and honey, and it is a seat for the people of Paradise. While they were in a gathering, angels from their Lord came to them, leading camels bridled with chains of gold. Their faces were like lamps because of their beauty, and their hair was like the silk of a mar’aziz because of its softness. Upon them were saddles, their planks were of ruby, their tambourines were of gold, and their clothes were of fine silk and brocade. They would dismount them and say, Our Lord has sent us to you so that you may visit Him and greet Him. He said, So they would ride them. He said, “They are faster than a bird and softer than a moth, riding horses without a profession. A man would walk beside his brother while he spoke to him and confided in him. The ear of one of them would not touch the ear of its companion, nor would the kneeling of a camel touch the kneeling of its companion. Even a tree would move out of their way so as not to separate a man from his brother. He said, “So they would come to the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and He would reveal His Noble Face to them so that they could look at Him. When they saw Him, they would say, ‘O God, You are peace, and from You is peace, and glory and honor are due to You.’” He said: Then the Blessed and Exalted will say: I am peace and from me peace, and upon you is my mercy and love. Welcome to my servants who feared me in secret and obeyed my command. He said: Then they will say: Our Lord, we did not worship you as you should be worshipped, and we did not appreciate you as you should be appreciated, so give us permission to prostrate before you. He said: Then God will say: It is not a house of hardship or worship, but rather a house of sovereignty and bliss, and I have lifted the hardship of worship from you, so ask me whatever you wish, for every man among you has a wish. So they will ask Him, and even the shortest of them will say: My Lord, the people of this world compete in their worldly life and are distressed by it. My Lord, give me everything that is less than your status. This is from me for you, and I will honor you with my status, for in my giving there is no hardship or restriction. He said: Then He will say: Offer to my servants that which their wishes have not reached and has not crossed their minds. He said: They will be shown to them until they fulfil their desires that are in their souls. Among what they will be shown to them will be two horned mules, for every four of them there will be a bed of a single ruby, over each bed there will be a dome of hollowed gold, in each dome there will be furniture from the furniture of Paradise, in each dome there will be two maidens from the houris, on each maiden there will be two garments from the garments of Paradise, there will be no colour except that it is in them, and no pleasant scent except that it has been perfumed with them. The light of their faces will penetrate the thickness of the dome, until whoever sees them will think that they are below the dome. He will see their brains from above their legs like a white thread of red ruby. They will see him as having more superiority over his companion than the sun has over stones, or better, and he will see their terror like that. Then he will enter to them and they will greet him and kiss him and embrace him and say to him: By God, we did not think that God would create the likes of you. Then God will command the angels to walk with them in rows in Paradise until each man of them reaches the place that has been prepared for him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ali bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Hammad, he said: A tree in Paradise, in the home of a believer is a branch of it. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hassan bin Abi Al-Ashras, on the authority of Mughith bin Sami, who said: Tooba is a tree in Paradise. If a man were to ride a young camel, male or female, and go around with it, he would not reach the place from which he departed until he died of old age. There is no house among the people of Paradise except that there is a branch of that tree hanging down over them. When they want to eat from the fruit, it hangs down to them so they can eat from it whatever they want, and the birds come and they eat from it whatever they want, whether dried or roasted, then it flies away. It was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that it was said by someone who said: It is a tree. The novel mentioned that: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Qumisi narrated to me, saying: Abu Tobah al-Rabi’ ibn Nafi’ narrated to us, saying: Mu’awiyah ibn Salam narrated to us, on the authority of Zayd, that he heard Abu Salam say: Aamer ibn Zayd al-Bakali narrated to us, saying: He heard Utbah, on the authority of Abd al-Salami, saying: “A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, are there fruits in Paradise? He said: Yes, there is a tree in it called Tuba, which is like al-Firdaws. He said: What tree of our land does it resemble? He said: It does not resemble any of the trees of your land, but you have come to Ash-Sham? He said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: It resembles a tree called al-Jawzah, which grows on one trunk, then spreads out at the top. He said: How large is its root? He said: If a young camel from your family were to set out, it would not reach its root until its collarbones would break from old age.” Al-Hasan bin Shabib told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Jazari told us, on the authority of Furat bin Abi Al-Furat, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurra, on the authority of his father, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Blessings and a good place of return’. It is a tree that God planted with His hand, and breathed into it of His spirit. It grew with ornaments and finery, and its branches can be seen from behind the wall of Paradise.” Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, that Diraj told him, that Abu al-Haytham told him, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, “on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that a man said to him: O Messenger of God, what is Tuba? He said: It is a tree in Paradise, a distance of one hundred years, from whose sleeves the clothes of the people of Paradise come out.” Abu Ja`far said: According to this interpretation that we mentioned about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the narration with it, the statement regarding the raising of his statement: Blessed are they, must be contrary to the statement that we narrated about it from the Arab scholars. This is because the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is that Tuba is the name of a tree in Paradise. So if that is the case, then it is a name for a definite noun like Zayd and `Amr. And if that is the case, then there is nothing in his statement: And a good return, except the raising, in apposition to Tuba. As for his saying: And a good place to return, he is saying: And a good place to return, like: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: And a good place of return, he said: a good place of return.
13:30: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Thus We sent you, O Muhammad, to a group of people - meaning to a group - before which there had been groups like them, so you went on, that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, meaning: to convey to them what I sent you with from My revelation that I revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful, meaning: while they deny the Oneness of God and belie it, "Say: He is my Lord," meaning: if these people to whom I sent you, O Muhammad, disbelieve in the Most Merciful, then you say: God is my Lord, "There is no god but He. In Him I have relied, and to Him is my return," meaning: and to Him is my return and my repentance. It is a source of the saying: I repented completely and repentantly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious, “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the time of Al-Hudaybiyyah, when he made peace with the Quraysh, wrote: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, made peace upon. The polytheists of the Quraysh said: If you are the Messenger of God and we fight you, then we have wronged you! But write: This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah made peace upon. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let us fight them, O Messenger of God! He said: No, but write as they wish, I am Muhammad ibn Abdullah. So when he wrote the letter: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, the Quraysh said: As for: The Most Gracious, we do not know it, and the people of ignorance used to write: In your name, O God. His companions said: O Messenger of God, let us fight them! He said: No, but write as they wish.” Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: His statement: Thus have We sent you to a nation that has passed on, the verse, he said: This was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to the Quraysh at Al-Hudaybiyyah. He wrote: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. They said: Do not write the Most Gracious, for we do not know what the Most Gracious is. Write only: In Your name, O God. God said: “And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious. Say: He is my Lord; there is no god except Him,” the verse. The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved or the earth could be split apart or the dead could be made to speak, but to God belongs the command entirely. Abu Jaafar said: The interpreters differed about the meaning of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious, “And if a Qur’an were to move the mountains,” meaning: They disbelieve in God even if He were to move the mountains for them with this Qur’an. They said: It is from the deferred which means to bring forward, and they made the answer to if come before it. That is because the speech is based on the meaning of what they said: And if this Qur’an were to move the mountains or the earth were to be split apart, they would disbelieve in the Most Gracious. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And if only a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak, he said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh. They said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If only you could expand the valleys of Mecca for us, and move its mountains so that we could till them, and bring back to life those of us who died, and by which the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak! God Almighty said: And if only a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak! Rather, to God belongs the command entirely. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak, the words of the infidels of Quraysh to Muhammad: Move our mountains so that our land may expand for us, for it is narrow, or bring Syria closer to us so that we may trade there, or bring our fathers out of their graves so that we may speak to them! So God Almighty said: And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Kathir said: They said: Even if the mountains were removed from us, or rivers were made to flow for us, or the dead were made to speak with it! So that was revealed. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: They said: The mountains were moved by the Qur’an, the earth was cut by the Qur’an, and our dead were brought forth with it. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Kathir said: They said: If only the mountains were moved away from us, or rivers were made to flow for us, or the dead were made to speak with it! Then the verse was revealed: Have those who have believed not despaired? Others said: Rather, its meaning is: And if a Qur’an were to move the mountains, a statement that is a new sentence separated from His statement: And they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. He said: The answer to if is omitted, and the listeners’ knowledge of what is meant by the statement suffices without mentioning its answer. They said: The Arabs do that a lot, and from it is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Even if it is a soul that dies suddenly, it is a soul that cuts off many breaths. It is the last verse in the poem, so he left the answer, satisfied that his listener knew what he meant, and as the other said: I swear that if anything came to us from his messenger other than you, we would not have found a defense for you. Mention of someone who said something similar to that: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak, he mentioned to us that the Quraysh said: If it pleases you, O Muhammad, to follow you - or: that we follow you - then move for us the mountains of Tihamah, or increase for us our territory in our sanctuary so that we may establish plots of land to practice therein, or revive for us so-and-so and so-and-so! People who died in the Age of Ignorance. So God revealed: And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak, meaning: If He had done this with a Qur’an before your Qur’an, He would have done it with your Qur’an. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The infidels of Quraysh said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Remove the mountains of Tihamah from us so that we may cultivate them and they will be our lands, or revive for him so-and-so and so-and-so who will tell us: What you say is true! God said: “And if there had been a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved or the earth could be split asunder or the dead could be made to speak. Rather, to God belongs the command entirely.” He said: If that had been done with any of the books in the past, that would have been it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj who said, I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And if there had been a Qur’an by which the mountains could be moved, that is, the infidels of Quraysh said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Move the mountains for us as they were made subservient to David, or divide the earth for us as it was divided for Solomon, so he could travel in it for a month and in it for a month, or speak to the dead for us as Jesus spoke to them, saying: I did not send down this as a book, but it was something I gave to my prophets and messengers. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, the verse, he said: They said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you are truthful, then move these mountains away from us and make them fields like the land of Ash-Sham, Egypt, and the countries, or resurrect our dead and inform them, for they died upon what we are upon! So God said, And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak, that has never been done with any Qur’an or book, so that is not done with this Qur’an. The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Have those who believe not despaired that if God willed, He could guide all people? Abu Jaafar said: Those who know the Arabic language differed regarding the meaning of his saying: Did he not despair? Some of the people of Basra claimed that its meaning was: Did he not know and become clear? He cited as evidence for his saying that the verse of Suhaim bin Watheel Al-Riyahi: I say to them by the people when they capture me, have you not despaired that I am the son of a knight who has asceticism? It is narrated: They make it easy for me. Whoever narrates it as they make it easy for me means: They divide me up, from gambling, as one divides up camels. Whoever narrates it as: They take me prisoner, means: Isn’t it possible for you to be taken prisoner? He said: He meant by his saying: Have you not despaired? Have you not known? They also recited in this regard: Did not the people despair that I am his son, even though I am far from the land of the tribe? They interpreted his saying: Did he not despair? Did he not know and see clearly? It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Al-Kalbi that this is the language of a tribe of the Nakha’ called Wahbil. They say: Did you not know such-and-such? meaning: Did you not know it? It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Ma’n that it is the language of Hawazin, and that they say: I despaired of such-and-such, I knew. As for some of the Kufians, he denied that, and claimed that he had not heard any of the Arabs say: I despaired, meaning I knew. He says: It is in meaning - even if it is not heard that I despaired means I knew - it is directed towards that, since he has made it clear to the believers that if he had willed, he would have guided all people, so he said: Have they not despaired of knowledge? He says: Knowledge has made them despair. So it is as if knowledge is implied in it, as it is said: I have despaired of you that you will not succeed with knowledge, as if it was said: I taught him knowledge. He said: And the poet’s saying: Even if the archers despaired and sent a flock of birds to destroy their husks Its meaning: Until they despaired of everything possible, except what appeared to them, they sent, so it is in the meaning: Until they knew that there was no way except what they saw and their knowledge ended, so everything other than it was despair. As for the people of interpretation, they interpreted it to mean: Did he not know and see clearly? Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Kufi, on the authority of a freed slave of Bahsr, that Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to recite: Have those who believe not become clear? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Hanzala, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Has he not despaired? He said: Has he not become clear? Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, Al-Qasim told us, Yazid told us, on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Al-Kharit - or: Ya`la bin Hakim - on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it: Have those who believe not become clear? He said: The scribe wrote the other one while he was asleep. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: In the first reading, Ibn Kathir and others claimed: Has it not become clear? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Have those who have believed not despaired? He said: Has it not become clear? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Have those who have believed not despaired? He said: He knows. Imran bin Musa told us, he said, Abdul-Warith told us, he said, Laith told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Have those who have believed not despaired? He said: Has it not become clear? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Have those who have believed not despaired? He said: Have those who have believed not become clear? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Have those who have believed not despaired? He said: Have those who have believed not known? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Have not those who have believed despaired? He said: Have those who have believed not known? Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement about this is what the people of interpretation said, that the interpretation of this is: Has it not become clear and known, due to the consensus of the people of interpretation on this, and the verses that we recited about it. Abu Ja`far said: The interpretation of the statement then is: If there had been a Qur’an other than this Qur’an by which mountains would have been moved, it would have been moved by this Qur’an, or the earth would have been split by it, it would have been split by this, or the dead would have been spoken to by it, it would have been spoken to by this. But that was not done with any Qur’an before this Qur’an, so He would do with this. Rather, the matter is entirely God’s. He says: All of that is up to Him and in His hand. He guides whomever He wills to faith and grants him success in it, and He misguides whomever He wills and abandons him. Did not those who believed in God and His Messenger, when they hoped for my answer to the one who asked their Prophet what he asked about moving the mountains away from them, bringing the land of Ash-Sham close to them, and bringing their dead back to life, realize that if God had willed, He could have guided all people to faith in Him without creating a sign or bringing about anything that they asked to be brought about? God Almighty says: What is the meaning of their love for that, while they know that guidance and destruction are up to Me and in My hand, whether I revealed a sign or not, I guide whomever I will without revealing a sign, and I misguide whomever I will with revealing it.
13:31: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve, O Muhammad, from your people, will be afflicted by what they have done, from their disbelief in God, their denial of you, and their expulsion of you from among them, a calamity, which is what befalls them of affliction, torment, and punishment, sometimes by killing, sometimes by wars, and sometimes by famine, or you descend, O Muhammad, he says: or you descend, near their home, with your army and companions, until the promise of God comes, which He promised you concerning them, and that is your victory over them, your conquest of their land, and your subjugation of them with the sword, Indeed, God does not fail in His promise, he says: God will fulfill for you, O Muhammad, what He promised you of victory over them, because He does not fail in His promise. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abu Dawud told us, al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by what they have done, he said: A military expedition. Or it will alight near their home, he said: O Muhammad, until the promise of God comes to pass, he said: The conquest of Mecca. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Masoudi, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar, except that he did not mention a raid. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Abu Qatan told us, Al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He recited this verse: And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by what they have done, a calamity, he said: The calamity is the military expedition, or it will descend near their home, he said: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the promise of God comes to pass, he said: The conquest of Mecca. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Zuhair told us: that Khasif told them, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And those who disbelieve will continue to be afflicted by what they have done, or it will descend near their homes, he said: It was revealed in Medina regarding the expeditions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or it will descend, you, O Muhammad, near their homes. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Al-Nadr Ibn Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah: And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by what they have done, a disaster will strike them, he said: a raid, or it will alight near their home, he said: you, O Muhammad. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement: And those who disbelieve will continue to be afflicted by what they have done with a terrible calamity, meaning: a punishment from the sky that descends upon them, or it descends near their homes, meaning the descent of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon them and his fighting them. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: A disaster will strike them because of what they have done, a raiding party will be struck by them, or a calamity will befall them - or Muhammad will settle near their home - and his statement: until the promise of God comes, he said: the victory. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh: Or it is located near their home, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Mujahid, similar to the hadith of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Shababah. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Qari’ah, he said: the raids. He said, Abdul Aziz told us, Abdul Ghaffar told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: A calamity, he said: A calamity from Muhammad, or it befalls near their home, he said: You, O Muhammad, until the promise of God comes, he said: The victory. He said, Israel told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: Qari’ah, he said: A battalion. He said, Abdul Aziz told us, Amr bin Thabit told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: A disaster will strike them because of what they have done, he said: A raid, or it will descend near their home, he said: You, O Muhammad. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by what they have done, meaning: by their evil deeds, and his saying: or it descends near their home, you, O Muhammad, until the promise of God comes to pass, and the promise of God is the conquest of Mecca. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A calamity, he said: A catastrophe, or you happen to be near their home, he said: He meant the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Or you happen to be near their home. Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Muhammad bin Talha told us, on the authority of Talha, on the authority of Mujahid: A calamity will strike them for what they did, he said: A raid. Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: A calamity will strike them because of what they have done, he said: the raiding parties, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would send them, or they will settle near their home, you, O Muhammad, until the promise of God comes to pass, he said: the conquest of Mecca. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Mujahid: A calamity will strike them for what they have done, he said: a battalion. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by what they have done, he said: A calamity of torment. Others said: The meaning of his saying: or it occurs near their home is that the calamity occurs near their home. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said, Al-Hasan said: Or it befalls near their home, he said: Or the calamity befalls near their home. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Or it occurs near their home, he said: Or the calamity occurs. Others said about his saying: Until the promise of God comes, it is the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ma’la bin Asad told us, he said, Ismail bin Hakim told us, on the authority of a man he named, on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: Until the promise of God comes, he said: On the Day of Resurrection.
13:32: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, if these polytheists among your people mock and ask you for signs, denying what you have brought them, then be patient with their harm to you, and proceed with the command of your Lord in warning them and making excuses to them, for nations before you mocked and passed on with My messengers, so I extended their respite and extended their term, then I brought down upon them My punishment and vengeance when they persisted in their error and misguidance, so see how My punishment was for them when I punished them, did I not make them taste the painful torment, and make them a lesson for those of understanding? In Arabic, dictation means prolongation. It is said: I dictated to someone if you extended the time for him. It is also said: I dictated to a lover because of their length. Therefore, night and day are called colorful because of their length, as Ibn Muqbil said: Oh, home of the living, insist on the seventy days, with colorful decay. The wide hole in the ground is called a mall, as the poet said: So I moistened every mind, eye, and corpse of the veins with the hidden angels. For the length between its two ends and its extension.
13:33: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: Is the Lord who is eternal, does not perish or perish, is responsible for preserving the provisions of all creation, is aware of them and what they earn of deeds, is watching over them, nothing is hidden from Him wherever they are, like one who is perishing and perishing, does not hear or see or understand anything, does not ward off harm from himself or from those who worship Him, and does not bring them any benefit, are they both the same? And the answer was omitted in that, so he did not say, and it was said: Is He who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? like this and that, sufficing with the listener’s knowledge of what was mentioned over what he left out. That is because when He, the Most High, said: And they have made for God partners, it was known that the meaning of the speech is: like their partners whom they took as gods, as the poet said: Choose between a tall, short, and broad-shouldered girl Is that you or the one who tears the veil and remains the last of the nights? Money waster and money gainer He did not say, and he said: A span of a span is a span: and between such and such, he was satisfied with his saying: Is that you or the one with the torn garment, and the indication of the report about the one with the torn garment is his intention in that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Is he who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? That is your Lord, blessed and exalted be He, in charge of the children of Adam with their provisions and their life spans, and God preserves their deeds for them. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Is He who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? He said: God is in charge of every soul. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Is he who stands over every soul for what it has earned? meaning himself, he says: He is with you wherever you are, so no worker works except that God is present with him. And it is said: They are the angels who are assigned to the children of Adam. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Is he who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? And over their provision and their food, so I am in charge of that, and they are My slaves, then they attributed partners to Me. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Is He who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? It is God who is in charge of every righteous and wicked person, providing for them and protecting them, then associating with Him those who associate partners. And His statement: “And they have attributed to God partners. Say, ‘Name them, or do you inform Him of that which He does not know on the earth, or of an apparent statement?’” God Almighty says: I am the One who provides for these polytheists, manages their affairs, and preserves their deeds. And they have attributed to Me partners from among My creation whom they worship instead of Me. Say to them, O Muhammad: Name these whom you have associated with in the worship of God, for if they say: gods, then they have lied, because there is no god but the One, the Subduer, who has no partner. Or do you inform Him of that which He does not know on the earth? He says: Do you inform Him that there is a god on the earth, and there is no god other than Him on the earth or in the heavens? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement: “And they have attributed to God partners. Say: ‘Name them.’” If they had called them gods, they would have lied and said something other than the truth, because God is One and has no partner. God said: Or do you inform Him of that which He does not know on earth, or of an apparent statement? He said: God does not know of any god on earth other than Him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: “And they have attributed to God partners. Say, ‘Name them.’” And God created them. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: “And they have attributed to God partners. Say, ‘Name them.’” If they had named them, they would have lied and said about that what God does not know. There is no god other than God. That is what He said: Or do you inform Him of what He does not know on earth? His saying: Or by the outward appearance of the statement, is heard, but in reality it is false and has no validity. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that, except that they said: Or with an apparent meaning, meaning: Or with falsehood, so they came with the meaning indicated by the word without clarifying the true interpretation of it. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his saying: On the apparent meaning of the statement, means on the basis of conjecture. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Or by an apparent meaning of the statement, and the apparent meaning of the statement is falsehood. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Or with an apparent meaning of speech, he said: Or with falsehood and lies. If they had said, they would have said falsehood and lies. And His statement: Rather, their plot has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, God Almighty says: God has no partner in the heavens or on the earth, but their plot has been made attractive to the polytheists who call upon a god other than Him, and that is their fabrication and lie against God. Mujahid used to say: The meaning of deceit here is saying: It is as if he said: He means their saying that they associate partners with God. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his saying: Rather, their plotting has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, he said: their saying. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. As for his saying: And they were prevented from the path, the readings differed in its reading. The majority of the Kufians read it as: And they were prevented from the path, with a damma on the sad, meaning: God prevented them from His path because of their disbelief in Him. Then the sad was made damma because the agent was not named. As for the majority of the reciters of Hijaz, they recited it with the opening of the sad, meaning that the polytheists are those who prevented people from the path of God. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about that, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings, each of which was read by imams of the readings, and they are close in meaning. That is because the polytheists were turned away from believing in God, and despite that, they were… They were turning others away, as God described them in His saying: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God. And His statement: And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide, the Most High says: And he whom God sends astray from attaining the truth and guidance by abandoning him, then there is no one to guide him to attain them, because that cannot be attained except with the success and assistance of God, and that is in the hand of God and to Him, not to anyone else.
13:34: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: For these infidels whose characteristics He described in this Surah, there is a punishment in this worldly life through killing, imprisonment, and the afflictions that God will inflict upon them. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, meaning: God’s punishment of them in the Hereafter is more severe than His punishment of them in this world. And it is more difficult, it is more effective than hardship. And His statement: And they have no protector from God, God Almighty says: And these disbelievers have no one to protect them from the punishment of God when He punishes them, neither a close friend nor a guardian nor a helper, because He, the Majestic and Sublime, is not opposed by anyone who would subdue Him, so that He would be freed from His punishment by subjugation, and no one intercedes with Him except with His permission, and He does not permit anyone to intercede for someone who disbelieved in Him and died in his disbelief before repenting from it.
13:35: Abu Jaafar said: The scholars of Arabic speech differed regarding the uses of proverbs. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The one who raises the example is his saying: Underneath it rivers flow, in meaning. He said: It is like saying: So-and-so’s adornment, his dark skin is such-and-such. So dark skin is not raised by the adornment, rather it is the beginning, meaning he is dark, he is such-and-such. He said: If an had entered into such-and-such, it would have been correct. He said: And its example in speech is: Your example is that you are such-and-such, and that you are such-and-such. And his saying: (So let man look at his food. I) from one perspective, is like the Paradise that the righteous are promised, in it: We poured out the water, the name is clear because it is returned to the food in the accusative, and is renewed, meaning: His food is I poured out, then we did. He said: The meaning of his saying: Like Paradise, is the attributes of Paradise. Some Basran grammarians said: The meaning of this is: the description of Paradise. He said: And from this is the saying of God Almighty: And to Him belongs the highest description, meaning: To God belongs the highest description. He said: So the meaning of the speech in His saying: The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised is that rivers flow beneath it, or rivers in it, is as if he said: The description of Paradise is a description of rivers flow beneath it, or a description of rivers in it, and God knows best. He said: Another aspect, as if it is said: Like Paradise, it is said: Paradise that the righteous are promised. He said: And likewise his saying: And that it is in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, as if he said: By God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and God knows best. He said: His saying: For what I neglected in the side of God, in the essence of God, as if it was said in our view: in God. He said: And likewise his saying: There is nothing like Him, the meaning is: He is not like anything and there is nothing like Him, because He has no equal. He said: And this is not like your saying to a man: There is no one like you, because it is possible that He has an equal, and by God that is not possible for Him. He said: And similar to it is the saying of Labid: Until the year, then peace be upon you both He said: And he explained to us that he meant: Peace be upon you both. Aws bin Hajar said: And the dead are noble, like trunks, covered by torrential rains. He said: The meaning for us is: like trunks, because he did not want to make a metaphor for trunks, then liken the dead to them. He said: And similar to it is the saying of Umayyah: Saturn and Taurus under his right foot, the Eagle under the other, and a lion under his watch. He said: He said: Under his right foot, as if he said: Under his foot, or under his right foot. He said: And the saying of Labid: I lost his mast and his guest, we roam its matter in the hand of the left As if he said: He ordered her to the north, and to the north, and Labid also said: Even if you throw a hand at an infidel It is as if he said: Until I fell into an infidel. Another of them said: He is one of those who are blind to his report. He said: The Arabs do that. He said: And it has another meaning: For those who responded to their Lord is the best, like Paradise, a relative pronoun, an attribute for them according to the first statement. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings about this is to say: The parable was mentioned, so he said: The parable of Paradise, meaning Paradise, then Paradise was described with its description, and that is because its like is its description, and its description is nothing other than it. Since that was the case, then the parable was mentioned and it was said: The like of Paradise, and its like is its description and the description of Paradise, so its description was like the description of the parable, and it was as if the speech was about mentioning Paradise, so it was said: Paradise has rivers flowing beneath it, as the poet said: I see the years passing by, taking from me as secrets are taken from the crescent moon. He mentioned the bitterness, and returned in the report to the years. His saying: Its food is permanent and its shade, meaning what is eaten in it. He says: It is permanent for its people, it does not cease from them, it does not disappear, and it does not perish, but it is fixed without end. And its shade, he says: And its shade is also permanent, because there is no sun in it. This is the outcome of those who fear God, meaning: This is Paradise, which God Almighty described as the outcome of those who fear God, avoid His sins, and perform His obligations. And His saying: And the consequence of the disbelievers is the Fire, means: And the consequence of the disbelievers in God is the Fire.
13:36: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And those to whom We have sent down the Book, who have come to you and followed you, O Muhammad, rejoice in what has been sent down to you of it, And among the parties are those who deny some of it, meaning: And among the people of the religions who are parties against you, and they are people of various religions, and those who deny some of what has been sent down to you. So say to them: I have only been commanded, O people, to worship God alone, and not to associate anything with Him, and not to associate anything with Him, meaning: I make a partner for Him in my worship, so I worship the gods and idols with Him, rather I sincerely devote my religion to Him, inclining toward truth, To Him I invite, meaning: I invite people to obey Him and sincerely worship Him, and to Him is my return, meaning: And to Him is my destiny. It is a passive participle, from the saying of the speaker: Ab, ya’ub, awab, ma’aba. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you, those are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they rejoiced in the Book of God and in His Messenger and believed in him. His saying: And among the parties are those who deny some of it, meaning the Jews and Christians. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And among the parties are those who deny some of it, he said: Among the People of the Book. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], but among the parties are those who deny part of it, of the People of the Scripture, and the parties are the People of the Scripture, and their partisanship brings them closer. And his statement: And if the parties come to him, he said: because of their partisanship against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said, and he said on the authority of Mujahid: denies part of it, he said: part of the Qur’an. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And to Him is the return, and to Him is the destination of every servant. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you, he said: This is from those who believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the People of the Scripture, so they rejoice in that. And he recited: And among them are those who believe in it and among them are those who do not believe in it. And regarding His statement, And among the parties are those who deny part of it, he said: The parties are the nations, the Jews, Christians, and Magians, among them are those who believed in it and among them are those who denied it.
13:37: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And just as We sent down the Book to you, O Muhammad, and some of the parties denied it, so also We sent down the judgment and religion, an Arabic judgment, and made that, Arabic, and described it as such, because it was sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was an Arab, so the religion was attributed to him, since it was sent down to him, and the parties denied it. Then God Almighty forbade him from abandoning what was sent down to him and following the parties, and threatened him for that if he did so, saying: And if you follow, O Muhammad, their desires, the desires of these parties and their satisfaction and love, and you switched from your religion to their religion, you will have no one to protect you from the punishment of God if He punishes you for following their desires, and you will have no supporter to aid you and rescue you from God if He punishes you, meaning: So beware of following their desires.
13:38: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And We have sent, O Muhammad, messengers before you to nations that have passed on before your nation, and We made them human beings like you, with wives to marry, and offspring whom they produced, and We did not make them angels who do not eat, drink, or marry, so that We would make the messenger to your people from the angels like them, but We sent to them human beings like them, just as We sent to those before them from all the nations human beings like them, And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of God, God Almighty says: And it is not possible for a messenger whom God sent to His creation to bring his nation a sign, such as moving mountains, moving a town from one place to another, reviving the dead, and similar signs, except by the permission of God, meaning: except by God’s command to the mountains to move, the earth to move, and the dead to come back to life, For every term is a book, meaning: For every term there is a matter that God has decreed, a book that has been decreed. He wrote it and it is with him. It has been said: Its meaning is: Every book that God sent down from heaven has a term. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: For every term there is a book, he said: For every book that comes down from the sky there is a term, so God erases from it what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Abu Ja`far said: This is, according to the saying, similar to the saying of God: And the stupor of death will come with the truth. Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, used to recite: And the stupor of truth will come with death, because the stupor of death will come with the truth, and the truth will come with it, so is the appointed time, for it is a book, and for the book there is a appointed time.
13:39: Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that: Some of them said: God erases whatever He wills of the affairs of His servants and changes it, except for misery and happiness, for they cannot be changed. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Bahr bin Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: God blots out what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: God manages the matter of worship, and blots out what He wills except misery and happiness, life and death. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Laila told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal Ibn Amr, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: God blots out what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: Everything except happiness and misery, for He has finished with them. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Yazid told us, and Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: Except for misery, death, and life. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn and Qubaysah told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Abi Laila told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: God blots out what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said, Ibn Abbas said: Except for life and death, misery and happiness.
