Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: God blots out what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: God decrees the affairs of the year on the Night of Decree, except for misery and happiness, death and life. Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: God erases what He wills and confirms, he said: Except for life and death, happiness and misery, for they do not change. Amr told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Muadh bin Uqbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said: I said to Mujahid: If you wrote me happy, then confirm me, and if you wrote me miserable, then erase me. He said: Misery and happiness have been completed. Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid - he said, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: God erases what He wills and confirms, he said: God sends down everything in the year on the Night of Decree, and erases what He wills of life spans, provisions, and destinies, except for misery and happiness, for they are confirmed. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said, I asked Mujahid and said: What do you think of the supplication of one of us who says: O God, if my name is among the happy ones, then make it among them, and if it is among the wretched ones, then erase it from them and make it among the happy ones? Hassan said: Then I came to him after that a year or more, and asked him about that, and he said: (Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn. * On it is made distinct every matter of wisdom.) He said: On the Night of Decree, whatever provision or calamity will be in the year is decreed, then He advances what He wills and delays what He wills. As for the decree of misery and happiness, it is fixed and does not change. Others said: The meaning of this is that God erases whatever He wills and confirms from the Book other than the Mother of the Book, in which nothing can be changed. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said regarding this verse: God erases whatever He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: Two books, a book from which He erases whatever He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Amr bin Ali told us, Sahl bin Yusuf told us, Sulayman al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: God erases whatever He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: The Book is two books: a book from which God erases whatever He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. He said, Abu Amer told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: The Book is two books, God erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that He erases whatever He wills and confirms whatever He wants. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Othman told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shuqaiq, that he used to say: O God, if you have written us as miserable, then erase us and write us as happy, and if you have written us as happy, then confirm us, for you erase what you will and confirm, and with you is the Mother of the Book. Amr told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said: Among the things that he often used to supplicate with were these words: O God, if you have written us as miserable, then erase us and write us as happy, and if you have written us as happy, then make us steadfast, for you erase what you will and make steadfast, and with you is the Mother of the Book. He said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hakima, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi: That Umar bin al-Khattab said while he was circumambulating the House and crying: O God, if You have written for me misery or sin, then erase it, for You erase what You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book, so make it happiness and forgiveness. He said, Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hakima, on the authority of Abu Uthman. He said: I think I heard it from Abu Uthman, similarly. He said, Abu Amer told us, he said, Qara bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Asma Abu Hakima, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, on the authority of Umar, may God have mercy on him, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, he said, Abu Hakima told us, he said: I heard Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi say: I heard Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say, while he was circumambulating the Kaaba: O God, if you have written me among the people of happiness, then confirm me in it, and if you have written for me sin and misery, then erase me and confirm me among the people of happiness, for you erase what you will and confirm, and with you is the Mother of the Book. He said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, that he used to say: O God, if you have written me among the people of misery, then erase me and establish me among the people of happiness. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: God blots out what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, meaning: He is the man who spends his time obeying God, then returns to disobeying God and dies in his misguidance, so he is the one who blots out. And the one who confirms: The man who commits a sin in disobedience to God, and he had previously done good, until he dies in obedience to God, so he is the one who confirms. Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Hamid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ukaim, on the authority of Abdullah that he used to say: O God, if you have written me among the happy ones, then confirm me among the happy ones, for you erase what you will and confirm, and with you is the Mother of the Book. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibrahim: That Kaab said to Umar, may God have mercy on him: O Commander of the Faithful, were it not for a verse in the Book of God, I would have informed you of what will happen until the Day of Resurrection. He said: What is it? He said: The statement of God: God blots out what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: For every term is a book, the verse, he said: God erases what He wills, he said: I abrogate what I will, and I do from the actions what I will, if I will I will increase them, and if I will I will decrease them. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Affan told us, Hammam told us, Al-Kalbi told us, God erases and confirms whatever He wills, he said: He erases from provision and increases it, and erases from life span and increases it. I said: Who told you that? He said: Abu Salih, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah bin Ri’ab Al-Ansari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Al-Kalbi came forward and was asked about this verse: God erases and confirms whatever He wills, he said: He writes down the entire statement, until Thursday comes, and everything that does not have a reward or punishment is removed from it, such as your saying: I ate, I drank, I entered, I left, and similar statements, and they are true, and what has a reward or punishment is confirmed. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, I heard Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, something similar, and he did not go beyond Abu Salih. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that God abrogates whatever He wills of the rulings of His Book, and confirms whatever He wills of them, but He does not abrogate them. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: God erases what He wills, he said: of the Qur’an. He says: God changes what He wills and abrogates it, and confirms what He wills and does not change it. And with Him is the Mother of the Book, he says: The sum of that is with Him in the Mother of the Book, the abrogating and the abrogated, what is changed and what is confirmed, all of that is in a book. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: God erases what He wills and confirms, is like his statement: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it, and his statement: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, meaning the entirety of the Book and its origin. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: God erases what He wills and confirms, what He wills, and He is the Wise, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, and its origin. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, God erases what He wills, that is, what He sends down to the prophets, and confirms, that is, what He wills of what He sends down to the prophets, he said, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, that is, He does not change or alter. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said: God erases what He wills, he said: He abrogates. He said: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: The Reminder. Others said: The meaning of this is that he erases those whose time has come, and confirms those whose time has not yet come. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: God erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, he says: He erases whoever’s time has come and gone, and what is confirmed is the one who is alive and continues to his time. Amr bin Ali told us, Yahya told us, Aouf told us: I heard Al-Hasan say: God erases what He wills, he said: whoever has reached his appointed time, and confirms, he said: whoever has not reached his appointed time. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, similar to the hadith of Ibn Bashar. He said, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: For every term there is a book, he said: The terms of the children of Adam are in a book, God erases their terms and confirms them, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. He said, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: God blots out what He wills and confirms, the Quraysh said when the verse was revealed: And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God: We do not see you, O Muhammad, having control over anything, and the matter has already been completed! So this verse was revealed to frighten and warn them: If We will, We can innovate for him from Our affair whatever We will, and we innovate every Ramadan, so we blot out and confirm whatever We will of the people’s provisions and their calamities, and what We give them, and what We apportion to them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Others said: The meaning of this is: He forgives whatever sins He wills of His servants, and leaves whatever He wills and does not forgive. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed, regarding his statement: God erases what He wills and confirms, he said: He confirms in the stomach misery and happiness, and everything, so He forgives from it what He wills, and delays what He wills. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct and most correct of the statements that were mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse is the statement that we mentioned from Al-Hasan and Mujahid, and that is that God, the Most High, threatened the polytheists who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for signs with punishment, and warned them with it, and said to them: (And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by God’s permission. For every term is a decree), informing them with that that His judgment concerning them has a decree established in a decree, and they are postponed until the time of the coming of that decree. Then He said to them: When that decree comes, God will bring whomever He wills of those whose term has drawn near and whose provision has been cut off, or whose death has come, or whose humiliation has come from being exalted, or whose wealth has been lost, and He will decree that for His creation, and that is its erasure, and He will confirm whatever He wills of those whose term, provision, and food remain, and He will leave them as they are and not erase them. In this sense, the hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, which is: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar told me, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Al-Layth ibn Saad told us, on the authority of Ziyadah ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God opens the remembrance in the three hours remaining of the night. In the first hour of them He looks in the book which no one else looks at, so He erases what He wills and confirms.” Then he mentioned what is in the last two hours. Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli told us, he said, Adam told us, he said, al-Layth told us, he said, Ziyadah bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala bin Ubayd, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God descends during the three hours remaining of the night, and He opens the remembrance in the first hour that no one else has seen, He erases what He wills and confirms what He wills. Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God has a preserved tablet that is five hundred years long, made of white pearl with two covers of ruby, and the two covers are two tablets of God, every day three hundred and sixty moments, He erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, he said, a man told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qais bin Ibad, that he said: The tenth of Rajab is a day on which God erases whatever He wills. The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And with Him is the Mother of the Book. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: And with Him is the Mother of the Book. Some of them said: It means: He has what is permissible and what is forbidden. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Muhammad bin Uqbah told us, he said, Malik bin Dinar told us, he said: I asked Al-Hasan, I said: The Mother of the Book, he said: The lawful and the unlawful. He said: I said to him: What is Al-Hamdulillah, Lord of the Worlds? He said: This is the Mother of the Qur’an. Others said: Its meaning is: He has the entire book and its origin. Who said that? Bishr narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: The entirety of the Book and its origin. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: A book with the Lord of the Worlds. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: The entirety of the Book and its knowledge. He means by that what is abrogated from it and what is confirmed. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, he says: And the sum of that is with Him in the Mother of the Book, the abrogating and the abrogated, what is replaced and what is confirmed, all of that is in a book. Others said about this: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that he asked Ka’b about the Mother of the Book. He said: God’s knowledge, what He created, and what He created, He works. So He said to His knowledge: Be a book, and it was a book. Others said: It is the male. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Abu Ja`far said: I do not know whether Ibn Jurayj is in it or not. He said: Ibn Abbas said: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: The Reminder. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: And with Him is the origin of the Book and its entirety. This is because the Most High, mentioned above, informed us that He erases whatever He wills and confirms whatever He wills, then He followed that with His saying: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, so it was clear that its meaning is: And with Him is the origin of what is confirmed and what is erased and its entirety in a book with Him. Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And it is established. This was read by most of the people of Medina and Kufa: And he affirms with a shaddah on the ba, meaning: And he leaves it and keeps it as it is, and does not erase it. Some Meccans, some Basrans, and some Kufians read it as and establishes, with a light pronunciation, meaning: writes. We have previously explained that the meaning of this, according to us, is: his written approval and leaving it to be erased, as we have explained. If this is the case, then confirming it is more appropriate, and emphasis is more correct than alleviation, even though alleviation may be interpreted in meaning as emphasis, and emphasis as alleviation, because their meanings are similar. As for erasure, the Arabs have two dialects for it: As for Mudar, they say: I erased the book, I erase it, erasure, and with it the revelation, and I erased it, I erased it, erasure. It was mentioned about some of the Rabi’ah tribes that they say: I erased, I erased.
13:40: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Either We show you, O Muhammad, during your lifetime some of the punishment We promise these polytheists for their disbelief, or We cause you to die before We show you that. You only have to obey your Lord in what He has commanded you to do in conveying His message to them, not seeking their goodness or their corruption. It is up to Us to hold them accountable, and to reward them for their deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil.
13:41: Abu Jaafar said: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Did not these polytheists from the people of Mecca who asked Muhammad for signs see that we would come to the land and open it for him, land after land, around their land? Do they not fear that we would open their land for him as we opened others for him? Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: We come to the land, reducing it from its borders, he said: Did they not see that We open up land after land for Muhammad? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Have they not seen that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders? He means by that what God opened for Muhammad. He says: That is its reduction. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: What you conquered from the enemy’s land. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said: Al-Hasan used to say regarding His statement: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders, it is the victory of the Muslims over the polytheists. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? He meant that the land around him was being reduced for the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They looked at that but did not take heed. God said in Surat al-Anbiya 21:“We come to the land, reducing it from its borders. So are they the victors?” Rather, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions are the victors. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Did they not see that we come to the land and destroy it, or are they not afraid that we will do the same to them and their land, so that we will destroy them and destroy their land? Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Hissain bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: We come to the land, reducing it from its borders, he said: Did they not see the village being destroyed until the population was on one side? He said, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-A’raj: that he heard Mujahid say: We come to the land and reduce it from its edges, he said: its devastation. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. He said: And Ibn Jurayj said: Its destruction and the destruction of the people. Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Farra`, on the authority of `Ikrimah, regarding his statement: Have they not seen that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders? He said: We destroy it from its borders. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: We reduce its blessings, its fruits, and its people through death. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: We will reduce it from its borders, meaning: the reduction of its people and its blessings. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: We reduce it from its borders, he said: in the souls, in the fruits, and in the destruction of the land. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Talha Al-Qannad, on the authority of someone who heard Al-Sha’bi say: If the earth were decreasing, your house would be cramped for you, but the souls and fruits are decreasing. Others said: Its meaning is: We come to the land and reduce its people, and we destroy them by taking them to death. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: We will reduce it from its edges, he said: the death of its people. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: Have they not seen that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders? He said: Death. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Harun al-Nahwi told us, he said, al-Zubayr bin al-Kharit told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: We reduce it from its borders, he said: It is death. Then he said: If the earth were to decrease, we would not find a place to sit in. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: We come to the land, reducing it from its borders. He said: Ikrimah used to say: It is the taking of people. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Ikrimah was asked about the decrease in the earth, he said: The people’s death. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Jarir bin Hazim told us, on the authority of Ya`la bin Hakim, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? He said: If it were as they say, none of you would have found a well to defecate in. Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: Ikrimah was asked, while I was listening, about this verse: Have they not seen that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders? He said: Death. Others said: We will reduce it from its edges, with the departure of its jurists and its elite. Who said that? Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Talha bin Amr told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The departure of its scholars, jurists, and the best of its people. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The death of scholars. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct interpretation of this is that of the one who said: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? with the appearance of the Muslims from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on it and their subjugation of its people? Will they not take heed of that and fear their appearance on their land and their subjugation of them? That is because God threatened those who asked His Messenger for signs from among the polytheists of his people with His saying: “We shall only show you some of what We promise them, or We shall take you in death. For upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the reckoning.” Then He, the Most High, rebuked them for their poor consideration of what they witness of God’s actions with their peers from the disbelievers, and they still ask for signs, so He said: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? with the subjugation of its people and their dominance over it from its borders and sides, and they do not take heed of what they see of that. As for his saying: And God judges, and there is no objection to His judgment, he says: And God is the One who judges, so His judgment is implemented, and He decrees, so His judgment is carried out. And if these polytheists from the people of Mecca bring God’s judgment and His judgment, they will not be able to reject it. What he means by his saying: There is no one to question His judgment, is that there is no one to reverse His judgment. In Arabic, the follower is the one who repeats something. And His saying: And He is swift in reckoning, means: And God is swift in reckoning, He counts the deeds of these polytheists, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is behind their recompense for them.
13:42: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Those who came before these polytheists from Quraysh from the nations that preceded them plotted against the prophets and messengers of God, To God belongs all plotting, meaning: To God belong all the causes of plotting, and in His hand and to Him. The plotting of those who plotted among them does not harm anyone except those whom He wills to harm. He says: So the plotters did not harm with their plotting except those whom God willed to be harmed by it, and they only harmed themselves by it, because they angered their Lord with themselves by doing so, until He destroyed them and saved His messengers. He says: So these polytheists from Quraysh plot against you, O Muhammad, and God is the One who saves you from their plotting, and the One who causes the harm of their plotting to befall them, not you. And His statement: He knows what every soul earns, meaning: Your Lord knows, O Muhammad, what these polytheists among your people do, and what they strive to do to deceive you, and He knows all the deeds of all creation, nothing of it is hidden from Him. And the disbelievers will come to know for whom is the final home, meaning: And they will come to know, when they come before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, for whom is the final home when they enter the Fire, and the believers in God and His Messenger will enter Paradise. Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed: So I read it as the people of Medina and some of Basra read: And the disbeliever will know, on the basis of monotheism. As for the Kufa reading, they read it: And the disbelievers will know, in the plural. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading in this regard is to read for all: And the disbelievers will know, because the report before that was about their group, and after it was followed by report about them, and that is His statement: We will only show you some of what We promise them, or We will cause you to die, and after that His statement: And those who disbelieve will say, ‘You are not a messenger.’ It has been mentioned that in the reading of Ibn Mas`ud it is: And the disbelievers will know, and in the reading of Abu it is: And those who disbelieve will know. All of this is evidence of the correctness of what we have chosen from the reading in this regard.
13:43: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve in God among your people say, O Muhammad: You are not a messenger! As a denial of you and rejection of your prophethood, then say to them when they say that: God is sufficient, meaning: Say, God is sufficient for me, “as a witness,” meaning: a witness, between me and you, over me and you, of my truthfulness and your falsehood, and with Him is knowledge of the Book. So, if the word man is read in this way, it is in the accusative case, in apposition to the name of God. And the people of the regions read it in this way, meaning: and those who have knowledge of the Book, meaning the books that were revealed before the Qur’an, such as the Torah and the Gospel. And the commentators interpreted it based on this reading. The narrator mentioned that: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me, he said, Abu Muhayyah Yahya bin Ya’la told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of my nephew Abdullah bin Salam, he said, Abdullah bin Salam said: It was revealed regarding: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book. Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us, Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi told us, Shu’ayb bin Safwan told us, Abdul Malik bin Umair told us: Muhammad bin Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Salam said, Abdullah bin Salam said: It was revealed about: “Say: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.” Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.’ So those who have knowledge of the Book are the People of the Book from among the Jews and Christians. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: And with him is knowledge of the Book, he said: He is Abdullah bin Salam. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement: And with him is knowledge of the Book, he said: A man from among mankind, and he did not name him. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And with him is knowledge of the Book, he is Abdullah bin Salam. He said, Yahya bin Abbad told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever has knowledge of the Book... Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And those who disbelieve say, ‘You are not a messenger,’ he said: the statement of the polytheists of Quraysh, Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book,’ people from the People of the Book who bore witness to the truth and acknowledged it, and knew that Muhammad was the Messenger of God, as it is reported that among them was Abdullah bin Salam. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Qatada: And he who has knowledge of the Book, he said: Among them were Abdullah bin Salam, Salman al-Farsi, and Tamim al-Dari. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada: And with him is knowledge of the Book, he said: He is Abdullah bin Salam. It was mentioned that a group of the ancients used to read it: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, meaning: with God is knowledge of the Book. It was mentioned by those who mentioned that about him: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Wahshiyya, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And with him is the knowledge of the Book, he says, From God is the knowledge of the Book. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, he said: From God. He said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: And with Him is the knowledge of the Book, he said: From God is the knowledge of the Book. And this hadith was told to us by Al-Hasan bin Muhammad, he said: Shababah told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, and with Him is the knowledge of the Book, he said: He is God. This is how Al-Hasan read: And with Him is the knowledge of the Book. He said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur bin Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. He said, Ali told us - meaning Ibn al-Ja`d - he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur Ibn Zadhan, on the authority of al-Hasan: And whoever has knowledge of the Book. He said: God. Shu`bah said: So I mentioned that to al-Hakam, and he said: Mujahid said something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, he said, I heard Mansur Ibn Zadhan narrating, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he said regarding this verse: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, he said: From God. He said, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And with him is the knowledge of the Book, he said: From God is the knowledge of the Book. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan: And whoever has knowledge of the Book, he said: From God is knowledge of the Book. This is what Ibn Abd al-A’la said. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan used to recite it: Say, Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book, meaning: From God is the knowledge of the Book and its entirety. Abu Ja`far said: This is how Bishr told us: the knowledge of the Book, and I think he made a mistake in it, and that it is: and whoever has knowledge of the Book, because his saying: and its entirety, is a noun, and a noun is not conjoined with a past-tense verb. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Harun: And with him is the knowledge of the Book, he says: From God is the knowledge of the Book. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said: I said to Saeed bin Jubair: And with him is knowledge of the Book, is he Abdullah bin Salam? He said: This Surah is Meccan, so how could it be Abdullah bin Salam! He said: And he used to recite it: And with him is knowledge of the Book, he said: From God. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Saeed bin Mansour told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about the statement of God: And with him is knowledge of the Book, is he Abdullah bin Salam? He said: That is sufficient, and this Surah is Meccan? And Saeed used to recite it: And with him is knowledge of the Book. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ibad told me, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, he said: And whoever has knowledge of the Book, he said: From God. Abu Jaafar said: It has been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that this reading and this interpretation are correct, but there is a problem with its chain of transmission, and that is what: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told me, on the authority of Harun bin Al-Awar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited: And whoever has knowledge of the Book, with God is knowledge of the Book. Abu Ja`far said: This is a report that has no basis among the trustworthy companions of Al-Zuhri. Since that is the case, and the reading of the regions of the people of Hijaz, Syria, and Iraq was based on the other reading, which is: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, then the interpretation that is based on the meaning that the reading of the regions is based on is more deserving of being correct than what contradicts it, since the reading according to what they agreed upon is more deserving of being correct.
